snippet.title: I Reverse Engineered Any Faceless Channel (Full Walkthrough)
snippet.description:
🚀 Get the Faceless Reverse Engineer in Final Phase 👉 https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai
🆓 My free skills (Next Phase) 👉 https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

I built a reverse engineer for faceless content. You give it a faceless video you love, and it learns exactly how it was made: the picture, the sound, the script. Then it rebuilds it your way. I tested it on a story short with over 12 million views, from a channel with about 157K subscribers, and remade it in Minecraft. Same story, same beats, my own words.

👀 1. What it sees
It goes through the picture frame by frame: every cut and what kind of cut it is (hard cut, zoom, flash, fade), how long every shot holds, and what the camera is doing vs what's moving inside the picture. Then Claude looks at sheets of frames and works out what made each shot, because every method leaves a fingerprint:
• 3D render: shadows that obey physics, objects that keep their exact shape.
• AI video: it melts a little and messes up text and hands.
• AI pictures moved in code: the whole picture moves as one flat piece, nothing inside ever blinks.

👂 2. What it hears
It splits the voice from the music and the sound effects, times every hit, whoosh and boom against the picture, and measures the loudness so yours doesn't come out quieter than theirs. That's where my sound list came from: a handbell, knocks on the door, wind, a crowd, a shovel and a rooster at sunrise.

📖 3. What it reads
Every word with its timing, every bit of on-screen text, and the script as a whole. Across 27 of their shorts:
• about 58 seconds and 220 words, read at about 226 words a minute
• in 14 of 27, the first sentence is a person doing something (not a fact)
• "You see," shows up in 18 of them
• the explanation is saved for the end, so you have to stay to get it
A lot of their biggest shorts start from a fact that already blew up on Zack D. Films (the grave bell one from a short with about 109 million views), turned into a story without copying the wording.

🧱 4. How it rebuilds
Every kind of shot gets matched to something that can make it: motion graphics in code, 3D in Blender. For this one, every scene is built in Blender out of Minecraft's own blocks and textures, lit like a film, not like gameplay. When it can't build something on its own, it doesn't fake it: it writes you the exact image or video prompt to make it in your own tools. At the end it checks itself, with your video measured against the original's numbers.

It gets you the look, the sound and the pacing. It doesn't get you the idea, which is why Final Phase is focused so much on story and scripting.

GTA 6 is out, and everybody posting it starts from zero. Here are the 6 best GTA 6 Shorts niches (+ 1 bonus), each with channels already doing hundreds of millions of views, plus Niche Machine: drop in your gameplay, pick the niche, and Claude edits the Short. It runs on your computer, and can cost $0.

🎮 The 7 niches (and what Niche Machine does for each)
1. Commentary: talk over gameplay, captions in the middle, a picture pops up every time you name something. You don't even have to talk about GTA: RealSlip has 186M+ views talking Among Us over Minecraft parkour.
→ Give it a topic or your script ("make me a commentary Short about the GTA 6 map using my driving footage"). It writes and voices the script for free, picks a stretch where you're moving and adds the captions and pictures.
2. Game comparisons: Game Forensics has half a billion+ views. Their GTA 6 vs Sleeping Dogs Short has 7M+.
→ Give it two clips of the same thing. It finds the same moment in both and stacks them (GTA 6 on top), with labels and a title. Plus a list of comparisons to film first.
3. Stunts: Leonida Stunts has 960M+ views. The plane through two train tunnels alone has 73M+: the fails first, the landing at the very end.
→ Record yourself trying a stunt over and over. It finds every attempt and keeps the best fails, with the attempt number on each one.
4. Discoveries and myths: GrayStillPlays' top 3 Shorts are all called "Busting 5 Myths in GTA 5", 160M+ views between them.
→ "Give me 10 GTA 5 myths worth testing in GTA 6." You film the tests, it cuts them into the format.
5. Moments: fails and wild moments turned into a compilation, the way FailArmy grew.
→ It finds the bloopers, the fails and what's going viral, and puts them together. Add your own voice on top. (My bet for the one that does best on GTA 6.)
6. Rankings: Define Ranked has 142M+ views from just 42 uploads. Leonida Stunts' two GTA 5 rankings have 100M+ combined.
→ Give it 5 clips, or just prompt it and tell it which ones to use.
Bonus. Skits: GTA Gaming has 445M+ views of little stories with Franklin, Michael and Trevor. Franklin saving a shark stuck on the shore: 134M+.

⚙️ Setup
1. Download Niche Machine from the free Skool (link at the top).
2. Open Claude Code and say: "Hey, set up the niche machine skill."
Every channel in this video is listed inside the pack, with links.

💸 Run it for $0
• OpenCode (https://opencode.ai): a free, open-source version of Claude Code with free models built in. No account, no API key. The catch: the free models have a limit, so you'll run out if you make a lot of Shorts.
• Ollama (https://ollama.com): runs the AI on your computer. No account, no limit, $0. It still needs Wi-Fi to grab clips from YouTube.
1. Check your memory, not your storage. 16 GB → Qwen 3.5 9B. 32 GB or more → Qwen 3.5 27B.
2. In Ollama's settings, set the context length to 32k or more (the default is too small).
3. Open Terminal, type ollama launch claude, pick your model, then say "set up niche machine for me".
Honest take: a free model isn't Claude. It's slower and needs more back and forth, but it costs nothing. My tier list: Claude, then Ollama (depends on your computer), then OpenCode (only because of the limit).

⚠️ Good to know
• YouTube doesn't pay for reused content: a pile of clips with nothing of your own added. Add your own take, so it's actually yours.
• Only use clips you're allowed to use, and watch every Short before you post it.
• Most channels in any niche go nowhere. These formats are proven, and the game is brand new.

✏️ Correction: at 9:21 I say "135 million people watched". The shark Short has about 134.4M views.

snippet.description:
🔥 Black Friday Sale, get up to 65% off Higgsfield plans 👉 https://higgsfield.ai/s/higgsfield-seedance-2-5-4k-yt-jadm-h-tlZfaI
🆓 Both free skills (retro family cutscene + real-looking 4K film) 👉 https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

This video is sponsored by Higgsfield.

One sentence in Claude, a 30-second AI video out. A TikTok account got almost 19M views in its first 9 days with one simple format: a family moment played like a cutscene from an early-2000s video game. I turned that format into a free Claude skill, and made a second one for real-looking films. Claude plans everything, Higgsfield makes the pictures and three cheap 480p drafts with Seedance 2.5, then I make the best take in 4K on higgsfield.ai.

🔌 Setup (about 2 minutes)
1. Sign up on Higgsfield with the link above.
2. On higgsfield.ai, open the MCP tab, make sure Claude is selected and click "Add Higgsfield to Claude". Pick "Connect in the browser" and approve your account.
3. Optional: set Higgsfield's tools to "Always allow" so Claude doesn't stop before every picture. The skill still shows you the price before it spends anything.
4. Download both skills from my free Skool, then in Claude: Customize → Skills → + → upload them.
Higgsfield works best on desktop. They don't have mobile apps: any "Higgsfield" app on the App Store or Play Store isn't theirs.

💬 The whole prompt
"Hey, make one where the guest says no to grandma's second plate."
No style, no characters, no shot list. The skill already knows all of that.

🎮 What skill 1 (retro family cutscene) does
• The story: one family rule everybody in that culture already knows, played like a tragedy. A new shot every 2-3 seconds, every line written word for word.
• The cast: one character sheet per person (close-up, front view, side view), so grandma stays the same grandma in every shot.
• The look: it walks every picture back in time (a modern game, then an older one, then early 2000s: low-poly, mitten hands, blurry textures, orange haze). Ask for the old look straight away and you get real-looking people. It describes the look and never names an actual game.
• Then 3 drafts at 480p with Seedance 2.5, and you pick one for 4K.

💰 4K without wasting credits
A 30-second Seedance 2.5 clip is 90 credits at 480p and 840 in 4K.
3 drafts (270) + 1 take in 4K (840) = 1,110 credits.
All 3 in 4K = 2,520 credits. Drafting first saved 1,410.
Judge the drafts on the action, the camera, the faces and the order of the lines, not the sharpness. "Generate in 4K" makes the take again at full quality, so small details can change: put it next to the draft before you use it.
⚠️ Seedance 2.5 in 4K doesn't work in the United States yet.

🎥 Skill 2 (real-looking 4K film)
For when you want it to look real: a short film around one main character, or a nature-documentary moment. Same flow, drafts at 480p and 4K only on the take that works. This is where 4K really shows: zoomed in on the same moment, the 480p draft is a brown carpet and the 4K take shows the individual hairs.

💳 Which plan? Free, Starter, Plus and Ultra. If you make these every week, go for Ultra: all the models and 3,000 credits a month, and since the skills draft first, those credits go a lot further.

🏆 Higgsfield Community Contest: $1,000,000 prize pool, 20 winners, $200,000 for 1st place. Entries close Nov 26, winners announced Dec 3 👉 https://higgsfield.ai/contests/talent-contest

snippet.title: I Built a Free Tool to Edit Videos For 0$ Full Workflow (Turned Into A Free Skill)
snippet.description:
🌘 Final Phase: build your personal brand or faceless brand with AI, 18+ skills in one dashboard → https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about

🆓 Final Phase Lite + Papercut + all my free skills (free Skool): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

Editing videos with AI has one big problem, and it's not the AI: you can't see what it's doing. Is it rendering? Thinking? Stuck for 10 minutes? And when it's done, fixing one tiny thing means describing it in text and rendering everything again. So I built Final Phase Lite, a free window for the videos you edit with Claude Code or OpenCode.

👀 What it does
• Shows every step while the AI works ("Writing captions", "Rendering the final video"), with a clock, and warns you when nothing has happened for a few minutes, so you know when it's stuck.
• Plays your video straight from its files, no render. Scrub it, step frame by frame, like a normal editor.
• Pause, draw a circle around the thing you mean and type one line ("make this bigger"). The AI gets the exact second, a picture of the frame with your circle, and what's inside the circle. The preview reloads by itself on the same frame, and you watch the change land in your circle.
• You render once, at the very end. A box in the corner shows what every note costs, so you see your credits going before they're gone.

🎬 The real edit in this video
A 22-second clip of Alex Hormozi on The Diary Of A CEO about doing 100 repetitions, edited in Papercut (paper cards, words popping on as he says them).
• "make this bigger" went to Claude Code. It found the word in the circle ("repetitions") and made it about 50% bigger (110px → 165px) in about 40 seconds. The preview reloaded on the same frame.
• "make this blue" went to OpenCode with a free model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free). It changed one line, and the cost box showed 289k tokens · $0.00.

💸 Unlimited edits for $0
• OpenCode (https://opencode.ai): a free, open-source agent like Claude Code. It comes with free models: no account, no API key. Pick a model marked FREE in the window and every note costs $0.
• Ollama (https://ollama.com): runs the model on your own computer. No internet, no account, no limit. Tested with qwen3.5:9b. In Ollama's settings, set Context length to 32k or more (it starts at 4k, which is too small). Below ~9B parameters it's not worth it: use OpenCode's free models instead.
Small models are usually bad at editing because they have to go find the thing in your project. When you circle something, Final Phase Lite tells them exactly which lines make it, so they only change those.

⚙️ Install (no commands)
1. Download the folder from my free Skool (link at the top) and unzip it.
2. Open it in Claude Code or OpenCode and say "install this for me".
3. In any video folder, say "open Final Phase Lite".
It works with your Claude subscription, or for $0 with OpenCode or Ollama.

⚠️ Honest notes
• It's free and brand new. It does the job, but with a small model you'll sometimes need more back and forth than with Claude.
• Tested on a Mac. It's written to work on Windows and Linux, but that hasn't been tried yet (in the video I say "Mac and Windows").
• You type "install this for me" in Claude Code or OpenCode. Ollama is the model, not the chat.
• The "it may be stuck" warning in the demo was set off on purpose to show it. Everything else is a live run.

snippet.title: Dear GTA 6 I Vibe Coded Your Entire Game In 10 Hours
snippet.description:
🚀 Final Phase: build your personal brand or faceless brand with AI, 18+ skills in one dashboard → https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
🆓 All my free skills (free Skool): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

I gave Claude Code the exact same video game to build 4 times: 10 minutes, 1 hour, 3 hours and 10 hours. Same design document, same model (Claude Fable 5.2), and nobody touching the keyboard. It wrote the code, made the 3D models, made the music, played its own game to test it and handed me a finished game.

🎮 The game: DRIFTWARD
My own design, a space exploration game in the same genre as No Man's Sky. Walk an alien planet, climb into your ship, fly up into space and land on any planet or moon you can see. No loading screens, no missions. The brief asked for a cinematic look, a third-person explorer, a rifle, weather, day and night, and its own music.

📏 The rules
• Every build gets the same design document and runs on Claude Fable 5.2.
• Once I hit go, it's on its own. Nobody answers its questions.
• Free assets only, every one credited.
• No build can look at another build's folder, so they can't copy each other.
To be upfront, 3 things besides time changed: Builds 1–2 run in the browser (Three.js), Builds 3–4 in Unreal Engine 5 on a friend's PC. Builds 3–4 also got an endless galaxy (from a seed number) and more detail. Only the 10-hour build was asked for a Miami-style city with cars you can drive.

🧰 What you need (3 of the 4 are free)
• Claude Code: https://claude.com/product/claude-code
• Unreal Engine 5 (free): https://www.unrealengine.com
• Blender (free): https://www.blender.org. Claude doesn't click around in it, it writes Python scripts that build the models.
• Visual Studio Community (free): https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/community/. It compiles the C++.
My MacBook Air didn't have the ~100 GB Unreal wants, so Builds 3–4 ran on my friend's PC (Ryzen 5 7600X, RTX 5070, 32 GB RAM), controlled from my laptop.

📊 The 4 builds (from the build logs, costs at Fable 5.2 API prices)
• Build 1 · 10 min: done in 5 min 42 s. 1 agent, 14 tool calls, 588K tokens, 361 lines in one file, about $2.30.
• Build 2 · 1 hour: done in 50 min 44 s. 5 agents (a lead + 4 helpers), 298 tool calls, 33.7M tokens, about 4,000 lines, about $34.
• Build 3 · 3 hours: 7 agents, 347 tool calls, about 73M tokens, about 2,900 lines of C++, $61. A real Windows game: double-click it and it runs. Endless star systems, about 60–100 frames a second on the PC.
• Build 4 · 10 hours: 13 agents, 984 tool calls, about 324M tokens, about 6,400 lines of C++, $156. 8 landable worlds at home, a galaxy map, a beach city with traffic lights and cars you can drive, swimming, rain and snow.
Builds 3 and 4 started at the same moment on the same PC. Both hit my subscription's usage limit overnight and sat idle; when it reset, I gave back every lost minute, so both got their full time. Build 4 took 16½ hours on the clock for 10 hours of work.

🤯 What it did by itself
• Every 3D model (ship, rocks, trees, creatures, city buildings) came from Python scripts driving Blender.
• All sound and music was generated in code. No sound files downloaded.
• It playtested itself: launched the game, sent real keyboard and mouse input, and looked at its own screenshots to pick the next fix (28 screenshots in Build 3, 40 in Build 4).
• It had an AI generator for 3D models, textures and music signed in and ready. Neither long build used it.
• Both Unreal games are about half a gigabyte (511 MB and 497 MB). Nothing is stored: every planet is generated from a number as you fly to it.

💸 What it cost
All 4 builds ≈ $250 of API-equivalent usage. I didn't pay that: it all ran on my $200/month Claude subscription. Builds 3 and 4 alone came to $216.63.
Honest caveat: the jump from Build 2 to Build 3 is as much the engine and the PC as the time. The cleanest comparison is 3 hours vs 10 hours: same PC, same engine, same start time.

✏️ Corrections
• "8 worlds in each galaxy": the home system has 8 landable worlds; other systems get 5–8 planets and moons.
• "100 frames a second": Build 3 runs at about 60–100.
• Ground textures came from Poly Haven (Build 3) and ambientCG (Build 4).

🎞️ Credits
Unreal's free starter content (character model, rifle, walking animations). Textures: Poly Haven and ambientCG (CC0). Builds 1–2: three.js and Vite (MIT). Everything else was made by the AI.

snippet.title: I Made a Full Documentary Using Claude (Turned it Into A Free Skill)
snippet.description:
🔥 Black Friday Sale, get up to 60% off Higgsfield plans 👉 https://higgsfield.ai/s/claude-fable-5-2-yt-jadm-h-egBBFB
🎁 The free skill (Sodium Diorama) 👉 https://sodium-diorama.higgsfield.app

This video is sponsored by Higgsfield.

How to make videos with Claude: Claude Fable 5.2 directed this 3D documentary in about 50 minutes, and every 3D person in it was made with Higgsfield AI. Then, in one Claude chat with Higgsfield MCP connected, I built the skill's website live: an AI landing page where every photo and every video came from Higgsfield.

🔌 Set up Higgsfield MCP in Claude
1. Sign up on Higgsfield with the link above.
2. Open higgsfield.ai/mcp.
3. In Claude: Customize → Connectors → + Add → Add custom connector. Name it Higgsfield, paste https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp and sign in with your Higgsfield account.
4. Start a new chat and pick Fable 5.2 in the model picker.
Good to know: the Claude MCP connector works on any Claude plan (the Free plan allows 1 custom connector), but Fable 5.2 isn't on the Free plan. It's part of Max, and on Pro it runs on usage credits.

🎁 The 3-day trial
The trial is only available when you connect Higgsfield MCP to Claude: 3 days for $0 with unlimited generations on the top models. A payment card is required. After 3 days the trial becomes an Ultra plan at the Black Friday price shown during sign-up, unless you cancel.

🎬 How the film got made
• The look: everything is grey and silver, and sodium-orange light only shows up where someone is watching. It's written as rules inside the skill, so Claude follows them every time.
• The cast: for each character, Higgsfield makes one reference picture (1.5 credits), then Higgsfield image to 3D turns it into a rigged 3D model (44 credits). 6 characters = 273 credits, reused in every shot.
• The director: Fable 5.2 wrote a pose program (29 named poses, 3 checks on every person: feet on the floor, hips where they should be, hands on what they hold), split the film across 7 builders, then looked through its own frames and fixed what was weak. 38 out of 38 passed.
• The narration is a free open-source voice running on my laptop.

📊 Opus 5.5 vs Fable 5.2, same brief: 22 shots vs 36 shots, a cut about every 2 seconds. Fable also listed its own flaws: the paddle on the water and the opening shot of the island.

An AI that clips GTA 6 streams for you. 🎮 What it does, in 4 steps
1. Downloads only the audio. A 4-hour stream is a couple hundred MB, not a giant video file.
2. Listens to the whole stream on your computer: a transcript, where the streamer got loud, and (on YouTube replays) where chat suddenly sped up.
3. The AI reads the transcript 12 minutes at a time and picks what people share: first reactions, crazy discoveries, freakouts, funny fails, hot takes. Every moment gets a score, and anything that needs context gets thrown out.
4. Downloads only the minutes it needs, finds the facecam by itself and makes the clips, plus a caption and hashtags for each one.

📊 The real run in this video
TimTheTatman's GTA 6 Extended Look reaction stream: 4 h 09 min → 39 possible moments → the best 3 kept, in 13 min 48 s. It makes 3 clips per stream by default and runs several streams at once, so 7 streams ≈ 21 clips.

💳 Way 1: your Claude subscription (how every clip in this video was made)
Plans start at $20/month. No API keys. Everything except the picking runs on your computer.
1. Download the clipper from the free Skool and put it in your Claude skills folder (the Skool post has a paste-in prompt that does it for you).
2. Open Claude Code and say: set up the GTA 6 clipper. It checks what your computer needs, installs what's missing and tells you when it's ready.
3. Say: clip this stream, and paste the link. Or: find me today's biggest GTA 6 streams and clip them.

🆓 Way 2: free, no subscription, no API key
1. Install Ollama and Claude Code (both free).
2. Check your memory, not your storage: Apple menu → About This Mac → Memory.
3. 16 GB → download Qwen 3.5 9B. 32 GB or more → Qwen 3.5 27B. More memory = smarter model = better picks.
4. Open Terminal, type ollama launch claude and pick your model.
5. Same prompts as Way 1.
Honest take: the free model isn't Claude. It's slower, the picks are rougher, and expect some back and forth before you get clips you like. It still beats scrubbing a stream by hand.

⚠️ Good to know
• Mac only for now.
• Age-restricted YouTube streams (common with GTA) and Kick need your browser login: add --cookies chrome.
• Clip streamers who are fine with clipping, and watch every clip before you post it.
• YouTube ad money needs the Partner Program (1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours in 12 months, or 10M Shorts views in 90 days), and YouTube can refuse it for reposted, mass-made content. Add something of your own.

✏️ Notes on the intro
• The "2.5 million people / £400 million" figures come from Uswitch: a survey of 1,000 UK workers who play games, scaled up to about 2.56 million UK workers taking 19 November off, ≈ £403.5 million in work hours. An estimate, not a count.

• GTA 6 comes out 19 November 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, 13 years after GTA 5 (2013).

snippet.title: Everyone’s Making Claude Videos Now, Here’s How to Win! (Turned Into A Skill)
snippet.description:
https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
🚀 Final Phase: the 2.5D paper style from this video + the Reverse Engineer engine + 18+ skills in one dashboard. Watch the video on the page 

🆓 Free skills + weekly calls (free Skool): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

This is a new editing style for faceless content: 2.5D paper. Paper cut-outs on a desk, a big-head caricature with a sticker border, big words slamming in, and it moves like stop motion. I dropped in a reel I liked and didn't edit a single frame. I built it twice, once with Claude Opus 5.5 and once with Claude Fable 5.2, so you can see how long each took, what each cost and which one got the style right.

📄 What 2.5D paper is (4 things)
1. Flat: paper cut-outs on a desk or wall, seen from straight above or straight on. Depth only from shadows and layers. Not 2D, not 3D: 2.5D.
2. The character: a big-head caricature, a real photo with grain, a thick red sticker border, and a mouth that changes every few frames.
3. 16 frames per second, every frame different (normal video is 24 or 30). That's the handmade, stop-motion feel.
4. Words + camera: heavy words land one at a time, the caption box never moves, every scene pushes in, drifts, then whips into a hard cut. No fades, a new scene every ~1.5 s. The music drops out under the punchlines.

🍎 Opus 5.5: how Apple became Apple
• First version in about 45 min, but it looked like pictures with zooms on them, not the reference.
• My one note: look at it frame by frame, what you did vs what they did. It measured: camera moving 52% of the time vs 91% in the reference, real 3D movement 5% vs 39%.
• It wrote itself rules and rebuilt it as a 3D film in 25 min. Camera moving: 94%.
• Total: about 1 h 15 min, 58 credits (10 images, 1 AI video clip, 68 voices tested), about $25 at API prices, under $1 of my plan (about 1.4% of my weekly limit).

🕵️ Fable 5.2: Jensen Huang and the Nvidia story
• A second reel from the same page, a slightly different style. One prompt, carte blanche, no notes from me after that.
• Before building, Claude checked the story was real: Jensen Huang admitted an affair, Nvidia's board is investigating, and U.S. intelligence reportedly believes the woman works for China's spy agency (reported, not proven).
• An Opus 5.5 lead ran 8 Fable 5.2 agents: style analyst, writer, director, 4 builders at the same time, finisher.
• It went through all 754 frames of the reference and found it's flat paper seen from above, not 3D.
• It wrote 23 rules it could measure (cuts per second, camera movement, caption position, music level) and passed 22 of 23.
• It cut a "$200 billion erased" number it couldn't source, compared 69 voices for free on my computer, and fixed a colour bug nobody asked about.
• Total: 1 h 50 min, 32 credits (cap was 60), no AI video, about $68 at API prices (about $57 of it the 8 Fable agents), under $2 of my plan (about 4% of my weekly limit).

⚖️ Side by side
Opus 5.5: ~1 h 15 min · ~$25 · 58 credits · needed my note
Fable 5.2: 1 h 50 min · ~$68 · 32 credits · no notes
Fable cost almost 3× more at API prices, but used fewer credits, no AI video, and got the style right the first time.
To be fair: not a same-prompt test. Each model got a different reel and story, and Opus's reel really was more 3D (so at 7:06, "Opus didn't figure out it was 2.5D" isn't quite fair).

💡 My take
• Already have the skill and making a bunch of these every week? Opus is enough: cheaper and faster.
• Building a brand new style from zero? That's where I'd use Fable. Getting it right the first time saves hours of notes.
• Stickman animations? No need for Fable.
$ figures = my estimates from session token counts at API list prices. I'm on a Claude plan, so I didn't pay them.

🧠 The skill
This one isn't a free skill: the 2.5D paper style is for Final Phase members. Want your own style from a video you love? Reverse Engineer in Final Phase studies it frame by frame and builds the skill on your own Claude subscription.
🔜 Next video: the Alex Hormozi-style editor I showed at 9:23, and that one will be free.

• 7:56: I say Fable took about an hour and 15 minutes. It took 1 h 50 min (said right at 8:19).
• 8:10: "68 to 57 dollars" = about $68 in total, about $57 of that for the 8 Fable agents.

snippet.description:
https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about


🆓 Both skills from this video are free in my Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

Is Claude Fable 5.2 worth it for faceless content, or is Opus 5.5 enough? I skipped stickman videos (Opus or a cheaper model does those fine) and tested Fable on 2 things Opus can't really pull off: a Zack D. Films style short built in Blender, and a 3D documentary that Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2 built from the exact same story.

🐱 Test 1: Zack D. Films style, in Blender
• Opus 5.5 did the setup: installed Blender on my Mac, studied 3 reference videos frame by frame, tested how the 3D body bends and wrote the plan. Fable 5.2 (Medium effort) did the build.
• 27 seconds, 15 shots: a furry cat walks onto the keyboard, gets moved to its bed, comes back, rubs the keys and plants a flag on the laptop.
• Every 3D model is free (cat, laptop, lamp, desk, even the guy), the voice is made on my computer and it renders on my Mac: $0 on top of my Claude plan.
• Fur trick: 23 s per frame, so it tried a third of the fur, saw it looked the same and went 4× faster.

🏛️ Test 2: the same 3D documentary, Opus vs Fable
The story: the Panic of 1907, when a 70-year-old J.P. Morgan locked New York's bankers in his library until they saved the city.
• Opus 5.5: 23 minutes, about 40 credits, 12 scenes, about $10 at API prices.
• Fable 5.2 (Max effort, a bigger budget, told to go all out): 3 h 33 min, 245 credits, about $380 at API prices.
• What Fable added: 6 helpers working at the same time, 43 real public-domain records (1907 front pages, a 1901 map of New York, the Federal Reserve Act), its own rendering engine (motion blur, light shafts, a film look), 14 scenes, 25 bankers around the table in a library of about 13,000 books.
• It checked its own work: the first render had 20 seconds of black screen, it found why, fixed it and rendered again.
The $ figures are estimates from the token counts of my sessions at API list prices. I'm on a Claude plan, so I didn't pay them.

🌍 What people built on X (first day)
• Riley Brown: one prompt, a whole room built in Blender, 13 camera angles, rented 10 GPUs and rendered it in 4K in 52 minutes for $5.75.
• Alex Michael: a dinosaur nature documentary where Fable wrote all the code that drives Blender.
• A full YouTube explainer on how GTA's wanted system works.
• Same prompt, real bills: an ice cathedral cost $81.10 on Fable vs $45.97 on Opus (Fable finished 1 h 14 min faster), a glass pool $57.87 vs $14.39. Fable cost more in every test I found, and looked better in every one.

💡 My take
• Stickman, simple explainers, daily volume: don't use Fable. Opus 5.5 or a cheaper model does the job.

snippet.title: Fable 5.2 VS The Best Models 3 In The World (Full Breakdown)
snippet.description:
🚀 Final Phase: https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
🆓 All my free skills (free Skool): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

Claude Fable 5.2 just came out, and the price matters most. It's 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1, but still 2× Opus 5.5 per token. Per task, though, it can come out cheaper, because it uses about half the tokens. I compared it to the 3 models you're actually choosing between: Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) and Gemini 4 Carbon (Google).

💸 The price, in plain words
• Fable 5.1: $10 in / $50 out per million tokens. Fable 5.2: $8 / $40. Opus 5.5: $4 / $20.
• What you really pay is the tokens it takes to finish the task. On Vals AI (the first independent test), Fable used about half the tokens Opus did: about $18 vs $25 for the same set of tests, done in 44 minutes vs almost an hour and a half.
• On Anthropic's own coding test, Fable on High scores the same as Opus on Max for about half the money (about $7 vs $13 a task).

👨‍💻 Coding
Anthropic's test: real open-source projects, then would the people who run them accept the code? Fable 5.2 about 49%, Opus about 45%, Astra and Carbon a bit behind. Fable 5.1 was at 32%, so it went from last to first.
Which effort? Extra High gets that top score but costs about $14 a task (Opus on Max: about $13). High gets you Opus-level code for about $7, that's the sweet spot. Max scores LOWER than Extra High and costs about $45 a task, so don't use it.
On Vals: #1 of 127 models for building full apps from a prompt, Opus wins on fixing bugs that come with screenshots, and they're tied in the terminal.

🤖 Agents
Real freelance projects (Remote Labor Index): Fable on High about 41%, Opus and Astra about 21%. The biggest gap in the whole launch. Just using a computer (OSWorld): all close, Fable first, Opus right behind.

💼 Business work
Business workflows (AutomationBench): Gemini 4 Carbon is #1, Fable 2nd, Opus and Astra a lot lower. Office work (AA-Briefcase): Fable and Opus basically tie, Opus wins 1 of the 2 scores. Reading charts and graphs: Fable, Carbon and Astra super close, Opus is the weak one.

📊 The independent test (Vals AI Index)
Real-work tests like finance, coding, legal and tax. Fable 5.2 is #1 of 36 models, but by less than half a point: Sonnet 5.5 2nd, Carbon 3rd, Opus 4th, all basically tied. Astra is clearly behind. And on tax, Fable is #27. The top 4 are neck and neck, Fable just gets there faster and cheaper than Opus.

🏁 Model by model
• Fable 5.2: the hardest, biggest jobs (long coding projects, agents running for hours, research). Use High, not Max.
• Opus 5.5: still the everyday model. Half the price per token, almost the same coding. Anthropic says it themselves: start with Opus, go up to Fable when the job is really hard.
• Gemini 4 Carbon: best for business automations and the cheapest of the 4 on Vals. But you can't use it yet: only a small group of cybersecurity teams, no date.
• GPT-6 Astra: doesn't win anything here. The fastest on Vals, but behind on most tests, and it cost more than Fable on the Vals run.

🔑 How to get it
All paid Claude plans, in the apps and in Claude Code (type /model and pick it). It starts on Medium effort, so put it on High for the sweet spot. Launch promo this week: on Pro you can use up to half your weekly limits on Fable, and plans that already include Fable get 1 to 3 free resets depending on how long you've been subscribed. New fast mode: up to 2.5× faster, but double the price ($16 / $80).

🧠 My take
The first Fable that makes sense for normal people. Big builds, like a whole new editor skill: Fable on High. Everyday stuff (editing my videos, small fixes): Opus for now, until I test them side by side myself. Most launch-day numbers are Anthropic's own, so I'll make a follow-up when Artificial Analysis and Arena post their results.

📚 Sources (checked on launch day, Nov 9 2026)
Anthropic launch page: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2
Vals AI Index: https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/vals_index
Vals AI, Fable 5.2: https://www.vals.ai/models/anthropic_claude-fable-5-2

✏️ Correction
At 1:10 I say Gemini 4 Carbon "just got released". It's announced, but it's still not public: only a small group of cybersecurity teams can use it.

snippet.title: My NEW Viral AI Editor (Turned Into A Free Skill)
snippet.description:
🚀 Final Phase (Reverse Engineer: build your own editing style from any video you love): https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
Weekly calls in the Skool if you get stuck installing anything.

This minimal editing style is everywhere right now: classical paintings, a thick blue line, words that blur in right when they're said. People are charging for AI editors like this, so I built it as a Claude Code skill called Canvas and made it free 👇

🆓 Canvas + all my free skills (free Skool): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

This whole video is edited in the Canvas style (with some extra motion graphics on top), so you can see how it holds up over 10 minutes, not just a 20-second demo. Long format for YouTube, short form (9:16) for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

🎨 Why this style looks so expensive (4 things)
1. The face announces, the screen shows. When you start a new idea, you're on camera. When you describe it, the screen shows it. The face is on screen about a third of the time, with a new picture every 2.4 seconds.
2. The captions. 2 fonts: a heavy clean one, and a bold italic one for the special words. Take 5 words or less, make the most important one big in the middle, fit the small words in the gaps around it. Every word blurs in exactly when it's said, in 5 frames.
3. The scenes. Only a handful, and they keep coming back: classical paintings that slide in, real photos dropping onto textured paper, a thick blue line your words break in the middle, a dark graph where a glowing blue ball climbs one step per word, you as a rough blue cut-out, and the punchline as a quote on blue. Same paper, same blue, every time.
4. The sound. A soft cinematic track way under the voice, barely any sound effects, and the music drops out under the punchline.

⚙️ How I built it
The usual way is by hand: download 20 videos, screenshot 130 scenes onto a Figma board, then feed it all to Claude. That takes days. I pasted 1 link into Claude Code and used Reverse Engineer (my tool in Final Phase). It found the finished edit inside the video, went through it frame by frame (every cut, colour, caption and move), built the skill, tested it on one of my recordings, graded its own edit against the original and fixed it, 3 rounds. Link sent at 12:09, demo on my screen at 12:55. The short-form version took 7 more minutes, and it's rebuilt for 9:16, not cropped.

🎬 How to use it
In Claude Code, type /canvas and give it your raw video. It cuts your silences and mistakes, plans every line (face or picture), finds free public-domain paintings on Wikimedia, grabs your real thumbnails and photos, builds every scene, mixes the music and gives you the file. Your notes become rules in the skill, so every video comes out better than the last. It learns the edit, never the content: no one else's footage, face or words.

👥 Who it's for
• Creators making talking-head videos
• Businesses: a dentist explaining why you shouldn't ignore bleeding gums, and it instantly looks premium
• Editors and agencies: make this for clients in a fraction of the time

💸 What it costs
$0 on top of your AI subscription. Paintings: public domain (Wikimedia Commons). Photos: your own thumbnails and pictures. Fonts: free. Music: $0. Rendering: HyperFrames, which is free. No credits, no Higgsfield, no AI video generation. I run it in Claude Code with Opus 5.5. Building a new style is heavy on usage, but Canvas is already built, so you just use it.

📥 How to install it
1. Go to the free Skool (link above) and download Canvas: you get a zip and an install prompt.
2. Don't unzip the zip.
3. Open Claude Code, start a new session, pick your best model (I use Opus 5.5).
4. Copy the prompt, paste it in, press Enter. You don't even need to drag the zip in: the prompt finds it.
Stuck? Post in the Skool or join a weekly call.

snippet.title: How To Steal Any Editing Style With AI (Properly)
snippet.description:
🚀 Final Phase (all 18 skills in 1 platform + the Reverse Engineer engine): https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
Every AI editor I've given away came from reverse engineering edits I loved. Now I built the engine that does it for me: give it 1 to 3 reference videos, it measures the edit frame by frame and builds you your own AI editor skill in Claude Code 👇

🆓 All my editors + 18 free skills (free Skool): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Already in Final Phase? Open the platform and go to Reverse Engineer.
Weekly calls in the Skool if you get stuck installing anything.

🔍 What "reverse engineering an edit" means
Every edit is a bunch of decisions: how long each shot lasts, when it cuts and what kind of cut, when it zooms, the colours, how many caption words at a time and where they sit, which sounds hit on the cuts, where the music drops. Measure all of that and you can rebuild the edit without ever touching their footage.

⚙️ The 7 steps
1. Links: 1 to 3 reference videos (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or a file) + a name for your new style.
2. Measure: every frame, every cut and its type (new shot, jump cut, punch-in and how far it zooms), shot lengths, flashes, fades, black screens, colours, captions. The voice gets split from the music and effects, so it knows where the music drops, where the clicks, whooshes and booms are, and which cuts land on a word or a beat.
3. Look: sheets of every cut (2 frames before, 3 after), and Claude checks each one, because a flash can count as 2 cuts and a fast whip pan as 1.
4. Study: everything that makes the edit look the way it does, each claim measured or seen at a timestamp.
5. Build: your new editor, starting from the closest existing one (flash cuts → 1K Editor, colour chapters → Editor V3).
6. Test: it edits a raw recording of you in the new style, measures its own edit and grades it against the original, number by number, then fixes the biggest misses (up to 3 rounds).
7. Notes: you see the edit and the scorecard, and what you say becomes a rule in the editor, so it keeps getting better.

🧪 The test
Will Schafer's reel, the one behind Editor V3: 2 minutes, 2,901 frames, 83 cuts. It found the same things as the Editor V3 study: loudness -14.2 LUFS, the red, blue and teal backdrops, the cuts to black, the punch-ins and the booms. Then it graded one of my Editor V3 edits against the reel: 19 of 37 measurements matched. Pacing and sound match; the look (brightness, warmth, zooms) doesn't yet.

🛑 The rule
It learns the edit, not the content: never their footage, face, voice, music, logo or words. Only timing, pacing, structure, colours, text, transitions and how the sound behaves. Sounds it pulls from a reference are only a guide, and get swapped for free ones before a style is shared.

👥 Who it's for
• Creators: turn an edit you love (a vlog, a reaction channel) into your own editor, not a template.
• Businesses: a dentist sees a clinic's reel that performs and wants that look for their own videos.
• Agencies: a client sends a reel and says "make it like this". Build a style for every client.

💻 What you need
Claude Code (I use Opus 5.5 on my Max plan, so it's inside my plan). The measuring runs on your computer with free tools (FFmpeg, yt-dlp, whisper.cpp, Demucs, OpenCV). Works best on a Mac (Apple's built-in text and face reader). About 150 MB of study files for every 2-minute reel it studies.
Install: open Reverse Engineer in Final Phase → download the zip → copy the install prompt → paste it into Claude Code. Then fill in the "make a new style" prompt with a name and your links.

✏️ Correction
• 19 of 37: a re-run of the same scorecard later that day scored 20 of 37, which is what the platform page shows.

🙏 Credits
Reference reels shown for commentary: Will Schafer (@willtschafer), "The Life Cycle of a Creator pt. 2", and @vxwx8 on Instagram. Not affiliated with either. This video is not sponsored.

snippet.description:
🎁 Get the skill free in my Skool (open the post for this video): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

A channel posted its first video 10 days ago and already has 5.7M views. I turned its documentary style into a free Claude Code skill: true stories with a real map, real archive photos and real footage, built entirely in code on your computer. No video model, no animator, free local voice 👇

Weekly calls in the Skool if you get stuck installing it.

🛠️ How to install
1. Open the Skool post for this video and download the folder.
2. Open it in Claude Code and paste the install prompt from the folder.
3. Start a new session. Use Opus 5.5 (type /model to switch).
The first run downloads about 850 MB, once (the free voice, the word-timing model and the renderer), so make some space.
Then just ask:
• "Make me a documentary about the Titanic."
• "Find me a true story about the deep ocean."

🎬 How it works
My business partner Amine built a documentary skill: a real map, real archive photos, one camera that never cuts. I merged it with the Depth Theory look: "picture this, you are…", the side view of the ocean with the little "you" figure, big labels with green checks and red crosses, and the dive.
1. The story: give it a topic, or ask for a true story. It comes back with 4. I picked the USS Indianapolis.
2. The script: every line has a source. No source, the fact gets cut.
3. The voice: Kokoro, free and local. Or plug in your own ElevenLabs key.
4. Word timing: "12 minutes" hits the screen on the word, and the red circle lands on "exonerated".
5. Real material: only public domain or free-to-use photos and clips, and it labels footage that isn't the real event.
6. The beat table: every line and what's on screen, so it never goes static. It can stop and ask you at the story, the beat table and the final look, or run fully on its own.

💸 Cost
$0 extra. It ran on my Claude Max plan with Opus 5.5: no image credits, no video model, no paid voice. The Indianapolis film (1:38) took about 40 minutes from "find me a true story" to the finished file, footage and voice included.
Each film is about 1 to 1.5 minutes. For a 10 to 20 minute video, make 6 or 7 and join them as chapters. For TikTok, make one story and cut it into parts.

💰 3 ways to make money with it
• YouTube itself, once you're in the Partner Program (videos of 8 minutes or more can have mid-roll ads).
• Company stories: a 90-second documentary of how a business started. Even a dentist: the history of braces.
• Agencies: a new style to sell to your clients, or use it for your own brand.
I'm building an app that does the strategy part for you. It'll be in the Skool when it's done.

Then just ask:
• "Make me a Roblox short, when lil bro breaks the TV."
• "Tell the story of Nike, arcade style."

🎮 Skill 1: Roblox Shorts
Learned from the Offline Hearts format: the title on screen from the first frame, a moment every kid has lived, each family member reacting one at a time, a twist at the end. My first try looked like generic plastic toys, so I made 7 reference style sheets (overall style, kids, grown-ups, faces, house, props, format rules). They're the guardrails: same family, same faces, same house, every video. The sheets come with the skill. Real 3D in code, no Blender, music and cartoon sound effects made on your computer.

👾 Skill 2: Arcade Motion Graphics
From a 30-second McDonald's ad I found on Pinterest (8-bit game that turns into real food) plus a pixel loop in an old TV. Claude went through all 750 frames and wrote down every trick: the health bar shows how far we are in the story, the coin counter is what the hero collects, keywords pop in pixel type, and real photos get scanned into pixels. Works for any story with a start and a win: a company, a product launch, a founder's first year.

🎬 Skill 3: Motion Graphics V3
From 4 reels I found on Pinterest. I didn't just copy the look, I measured how much the screen moves, so it copies the energy too. Real people cut out rising out of cards with their name behind them, real pages with the exact words highlighted, every word lands the moment it's said. 9:16 for Shorts, 16:9 for YouTube, AI voice or your own recording, and your face can be one of the scenes. Runs locally, $0.

• The "mom's car" short took about 17 minutes from my message to the finished file, not 15.

snippet.title: I Found A Way To Make These AI Animations For $0 (No Subscription)
snippet.description:
A free open model (GLM 5.3 Flash) inside OpenCode built this 28-second stick figure video: the voice, the animation and the sound, horizontal and vertical. OpenCode's bill: $0.00. Here's how to make yours step by step, the free skill that makes it work, and the catch with free models 👇

🎁 The free skill + install prompt, in my Skool, in the post for this video: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790/classroom/2a43afcd?md=4a1aad81061942e4923bcd05da2ac24d
Free community + weekly calls if you get stuck: 

🔎 What "$0" means
$0 is what OpenCode charged. No subscription, no credits, no API key, no ElevenLabs, no account. In my test, Claude wrote the story and shot list, wrote the 11 notes and did a last polish on the video you see. Free ChatGPT and your own eyes can do those jobs, but that exact route isn't the one I ran.

📝 Step 1: the ChatGPT prompt
Write me a 30-second "What if...?" story for a stick figure faceless video. My idea: [YOUR IDEA]. About 60 words of narration. Short sentences, 1 idea per sentence, written to be read out loud. End on a question. Then give me a shot list: about 15 shots, 1 line each, saying which sentence it goes with and what we see on screen. If you use a real number, give me the source.

Keep the text, you'll paste it later. If it gives you a real number, open the source and check it.

🛠️ Step 2: OpenCode
1. Paste this in your terminal and hit enter:
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
On Windows, OpenCode recommends WSL: https://opencode.ai/docs/windows-wsl
2. Open a new terminal, type opencode, hit enter. No sign in. If you see connect, skip it.
3. Type /models, search free, pick GLM 5.3 Flash Free. If it's missing on your first launch, wait a moment and open /models again. Press Control + T until you see high.

🎬 Step 3: the skill + your first video
1. In the Skool post, open the Google Drive and download the faceless videos zip. Leave it in Downloads. Don't unzip it.
2. Paste the install prompt into OpenCode. It says Claude Code inside, that's fine: OpenCode reads the same folder. About 1 GB. Wait for SELFTEST PASSED and skip the music model (15 GB). I set mine up in Claude Code, so if it stalls in OpenCode, post it in the Skool.
3. Type /new, paste your story and shots, and say "make this a 30 second stickman video, horizontal and vertical." It shows a plan. Say go.
Stickman is the style I tested on the free model, so start there.

💡 Tips
30 seconds, 1 video at a time. Give it the full story and shots, not 1 line. Give notes with timestamps. Watch it yourself: it can say everything looks good when it doesn't.

⚠️ The catch + prices (checked Nov 1)
Free models are free "for a limited time" (https://opencode.ai/docs/zen) and I couldn't find the limit published. I hit it in under 1 hour with 2 videos running, and 3 hours later it still hadn't come back.
• OpenCode Go: $10 a month: https://opencode.ai/go
• Pay as you go, GLM 5.3 Flash: 15¢ in / 50¢ out / 3¢ cached per million tokens, plus 4.6% + $0.31 on each credit purchase
• "100 videos" and "60 cents" are my math from 1 test, not a promise
• The $149 tool is faceless.video's Studio plan

✏️ More exact than what I said
• Higgsfield: 4 of the 5 styles are 100% code. Clay Atlas needs about 12 stills from any image tool.
• Windows: it needs Google Chrome installed. That's what the skill is built for, but I've only run it on my Mac.
• Computer: the model runs on OpenCode's servers, but the voice and the render run on yours, so a slower computer takes longer. Mine is a 16 GB MacBook Air.

📎 The shorts in the hook are from Ricks Clips, not affiliated: https://www.youtube.com/@RicksClips3000 (30.4M and 15.6M views on Nov 1). Their numbers, not a promise of views.
Not sponsored by OpenCode or GLM. Nobody paid me for this.

snippet.title: The New Viral AI Editor (Turned it Into a Free Skill)
snippet.description:
Claude Code turned my raw footage into these 2 edits, and I turned both into free skills. Editor V2 is a fast picture montage learned frame by frame from 1 Instagram reel of 9 seconds. Editor V3 is a cinematic side silhouette learned from a reel by Will Schafer. Here's each edit next to the raw footage, how to install them, the version I threw away and what every version cost 👇

🎁 Both skills, free in my Skool, in the post for this video: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Stuck? Post it in the Skool and I'll reply, or come to the weekly calls.

⚡ Higgsfield, only for Editor V3 (you connect it to Claude once): https://higgsfield.ai/s/make-your-first-ai-video-yt-jadm-h-NEGQVt

🧰 What you need
Claude Code, at least $20 a month. I built both on Opus 5.5 and haven't tested a free model yet. Editing is heavy, so a smaller plan hits its limit faster. No coding: I didn't write a single line.

🛠️ Install (once)
1. Open the Skool post, download the zip and leave it in your Downloads folder. Don't unzip it.
2. Open Claude Code, paste the setup prompt from the Google Drive and hit enter. It finds the zip and installs the free tools (FFmpeg, a speech model, a renderer). If it asks to allow something, click allow.
3. Type "give me a demo of 10 seconds" to see how it looks, then start a new session.

🎬 How to use them
Drag in your recording and type 1 line: "Edit this video with Editor V2" (or V3). A few clips of you working help. Before V3 spends a credit, it opens a page in your browser with every shot and what it costs. Give notes with the exact second, and start short. The study tool comes with it, so you can give it any reel you love.

⚙️ Editor V2
About 30 pictures from the reel, used about 75 times, blurred or recolored each time one comes back. Claude cuts my voice, finds footage (Wikimedia Commons, Prelinger Archives), builds the montage on the reel's timing and places every sound. The first montage changed 11 times a second against the reel's 18. Now it's 17. The first full cut took a little over an hour and I didn't touch a clip.

🌑 Editor V3
I recorded twice: front for my voice, side for my outline and mouth. Higgsfield changes the light and background, so it's still my real take. 3 models on the same 5 seconds:
• Genjutsu: 7 credits a second, my mouth followed less clearly
• Seedance: 7.6, left a piece of my mic in the corner
• Kling: 2, kept my mouth moving. That's the one in the skill.
Everything after that runs on my Mac.

💥 The bloopers
Before these I tried a "1K Editor" and told Claude to use its imagination. A narrator came out of nowhere and my monitor flew at my face. Every time it imagined, it looked like AI slop, so I gave it 1 reel to learn instead.

💸 What it cost
• 1K Editor, thrown away: 812 Higgsfield credits. The Editor V3 edit says 1,000. I checked, it's 812.
• Editor V3: 217 credits. 127 were my model tests, which you skip. 90 were the final clips for a video a little over 1 minute, about 2 credits per second of silhouette.
• Editor V2: 0 new credits. The X-rays of my head are AI images from the 1K round, about 1 credit each, already inside that 812.

Claude Code turned my raw footage into these 2 edits, and I turned both into free skills. Editor V2 is a fast picture montage learned frame by frame from 1 Instagram reel of 9 seconds. Editor V3 is a cinematic side silhouette learned from a reel by Will Schafer. Here's each edit next to the raw footage, how to install them, the version I threw away and what every version cost 👇

🎁 Both skills, free in my Skool, in the post for this video: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

⚡ Higgsfield, only for Editor V3 (you connect it to Claude once): https://higgsfield.ai/s/make-your-first-ai-video-yt-jadm-h-NEGQVt

🧰 What you need
Claude Code, at least $20 a month. I built both on Opus 5.5 and haven't tested a free model yet. Editing is heavy, so a smaller plan hits its limit faster. No coding: I didn't write a single line.

🛠️ Install (once)
1. Open the Skool post, download the zip and leave it in your Downloads folder. Don't unzip it.
2. Open Claude Code, paste the setup prompt from the Google Drive and hit enter. It finds the zip and installs the free tools (FFmpeg, a speech model, a renderer). If it asks to allow something, click allow.
3. Type "give me a demo of 10 seconds" to see how it looks, then start a new session.

🎬 How to use them
Drag in your recording and type 1 line: "Edit this video with Editor V2" (or V3). A few clips of you working help. Before V3 spends a credit, it opens a page in your browser with every shot and what it costs. Give notes with the exact second, and start short. The study tool comes with it, so you can give it any reel you love.

⚙️ Editor V2
About 30 pictures from the reel, used about 75 times, blurred or recolored each time one comes back. Claude cuts my voice, finds footage (Wikimedia Commons, Prelinger Archives), builds the montage on the reel's timing and places every sound. The first montage changed 11 times a second against the reel's 18. Now it's 17. The first full cut took a little over an hour and I didn't touch a clip.

🌑 Editor V3
I recorded twice: front for my voice, side for my outline and mouth. Higgsfield changes the light and background, so it's still my real take. 3 models on the same 5 seconds:
• Genjutsu: 7 credits a second, my mouth followed less clearly
• Seedance: 7.6, left a piece of my mic in the corner
• Kling: 2, kept my mouth moving. That's the one in the skill.
Everything after that runs on my Mac.

💥 The bloopers
Before these I tried a "1K Editor" and told Claude to use its imagination. A narrator came out of nowhere and my monitor flew at my face. Every time it imagined, it looked like AI slop, so I gave it 1 reel to learn instead.

💸 What it cost
• 1K Editor, thrown away: 812 Higgsfield credits. The Editor V3 edit says 1,000. I checked, it's 812.
• Editor V3: 217 credits. 127 were my model tests, which you skip. 90 were the final clips for a video a little over 1 minute, about 2 credits per second of silhouette.
• Editor V2: 0 new credits. The X-rays of my head are AI images from the 1K round, about 1 credit each, already inside that 812.

snippet.title: Gemini 4 Carbon VS Opus 5.5 VS GPT-6 Astra (No Hype)
snippet.description:
Gemini 4 Carbon was announced today and went straight to #1 on Artificial Analysis: Carbon 59, Claude Opus 5.5 58, GPT-6 Astra 57. That's a 1 point lead. So I skipped Google's own charts and put all 3 side by side on independent tests only: coding, agents, chatting, making stuff up, running a business, and what one task actually costs you 👇

🎁 My free Claude skills (new ones every week): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

Not sponsored. None of these are my own tests or Google's numbers: everything comes from independent leaderboards (sources below).

📊 The tests (checked Oct 28, 2026)
1. Overall, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0: Carbon 59, Opus 5.5 58, Astra 57. Basically a 3-way tie.
2. Coding, AA Coding Agent Index (each model inside a real coding tool): Opus 5.5 in Claude Code 62, Carbon in Antigravity CLI 59, Astra in Codex 55. WebDev Arena (people vote on sites and apps without knowing which model built them): Opus #1, Astra #2, Carbon #4.
3. Side by side, a 3D helicopter from the same prompt (LuminaBench, early Carbon): Carbon took a bit over 30 min, Opus 55. They preferred Carbon's design but called Opus more polished overall. Not the same setup: Opus ran in Claude Code, Carbon on Arena.
4. Agents, Agent Arena: Opus #1, Carbon #2, Astra #4. A typical task: Opus about $6.70 and 19 min, Carbon about $1.80 and 12 min (at Google's 50% launch price), Astra about $5.10 and 11 min.
5. Chatting, Text Arena (blind votes): Carbon #1, Opus #3, Astra #37.
6. Making stuff up, AA-Omniscience hallucination rate (when it doesn't know, how often it makes up an answer, lower is better): Carbon 11%, Opus 50%, Astra 50%.
7. Running a business, Andon Labs' Vending-Bench 2 (a vending machine business for a simulated year): Carbon $16,484, Astra $15,515, Opus $9,235.
8. Price per 1M tokens: Carbon $4 in / $20 out, the exact same as Opus 5.5, and $2 / $10 right now with Google's launch discount. Astra $10 / $50. Cost per task at full price (AA): Astra $6.24, Carbon $7.76, Opus $10.04.

🏆 Who wins what
Carbon: overall (by 1 point), chatting, making stuff up the least, the business test.
Opus 5.5: coding and agents.
Astra: no category win, but the cheapest per task at full price, and #2 on WebDev Arena and Vending-Bench.

🔓 Who can use them today
Opus 5.5: Claude's paid plans.
GPT-6 Astra: ChatGPT's paid plans (Pro first, then Plus and Business, per OpenAI).
Gemini 4 Carbon: only a small group of cyber defenders (Google's Fairwind Program). Everyone else "as soon as possible", no date.

💬 My take
Carbon looks like the real deal compared to Argon. If you do research, writing or business stuff, I'd try it the day it opens, because making stuff up way less really matters. For coding, editing my videos and building the skills I share, I'm sticking with Claude. And launch day posts are always hype, so let's see what people say in a few weeks.

✏️ Corrections
• Gemini 4 Argon came out Sep 30, about 4 weeks before this video, not 2. It's still 8 points behind Opus 5.5 on the AA index (50 vs 58). Argon also launched to cyber defenders only, but it's open to developers now.
• Astra's cost per task is $6.24, not $6.25.

snippet.title: I Tried Kling 4.0... Has Huge Issues
snippet.description:
Try Kling 4.0 on Higgsfield 👉 https://higgsfield.ai/s/higgsfield-kling-4-0-yt-jadm-h-PCivIs

Kling 4.0 vs Seedance 2.5: same images, same prompts, 4 tests, 30 seconds each. Which one would you pick? 

Kling 4.0 is now live on Higgsfield, and it makes up to 30 seconds in a single clip, double Kling 3.0's 15. So a full 30 second AI video scene comes out of one generation. I put it against Seedance 2.5 in 2 realism tests and 2 animation tests to see if it can compete.

This video is sponsored by Higgsfield.

🎬 Kling 4.0 on Higgsfield
Higgsfield puts the top AI video generator models in one place, and Kling 4.0 comes with 3 modes:
• References: multi-reference video. Give it your characters, products and places (I used 8 images in test 2).
• Frames: keyframes AI video. Plan the shot with your own images (I used a start frame in tests 1, 3 and 4).
• Edit video: AI video editing. Change one part of a finished clip without redoing the whole shot.
And you see the credit cost on the Generate button before you commit.
Product page: https://higgsfield.ai/blog/kling-4-0-on-higgsfield

🧪 How I tested (a fair AI filmmaking test)
I made my reference images with Nano Banana 2.1 on Higgsfield. Both models got the same images and the exact same prompt: 30 seconds, 1080p, 16:9, sound on.
1. Realism: a dad waits on a snowy train platform with tulips, and his daughter steps off the train (Frames).
2. Realism, product ad: 4 friends, a hot tub in the snow and 2 flavors of Frostline, a made-up drink (References, 8 images).
3. Hand-drawn 2D: a flower seller opens his stall in a village square. Blind test, guess which one is Kling (Frames).
4. Anime: a bike courier races down a harbor town at sunrise to catch a ferry (Frames, one image, one prompt).

🏆 Results (my opinion, you're the judge)
1. Train: Seedance 2.5. Better sound and color, she runs and the train leaves. Kling 4.0 skips her run, jumps to the hug, and he says "There is" instead of "There she is".
2. Frostline: draw. Seedance looks more real but mixes up the cans and who opens what. Kling 4.0 looks more AI, but everyone grabs the right can. In both, they get in the hot tub with their clothes on.
3. Flower stall: Kling 4.0. It started on my image, every character showed up, the sign is spelled right and it ends on the pull-back over the rooftops, like I wrote it. Seedance skipped the lady with the dog (the dog talks instead). Kling gets blurry when things move fast.
4. Anime: Seedance 2.5. Better pedaling, the jump, the ferry in her eyes, and she hands off the package. Kling 4.0 has a great black and white impact frame, but she flips the bike and misses the boat.
Score: Seedance 2.5 wins 2, Kling 4.0 wins 1, 1 draw.

💳 What it cost
On my account, one 30-second 1080p clip cost 30 credits on Kling 4.0 and 480 on Seedance 2.5, so Seedance was 16 times the price. Prices can change with your plan or a sale, so always check the quote on the Generate button.

My take: Kling 4.0 doesn't dethrone Seedance 2.5, and Seedance still needs work too. If it has to be right the first time, Seedance. If you want to try a lot of ideas, Kling 4.0 is the better deal.

📂 All 4 prompts (start frames, the 8 reference images and the video prompts) are free in my Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

📝 Frostline is a made-up brand, and everyone in these clips is AI-generated.

snippet.title: My NEW AI Editor Completely FREE 0$ (No Subscription)
snippet.description:
🔗 Try Higgsfield: https://higgsfield.ai/s/video-model-showdown-kling-4-jadm-h-cJsSBE

🎁 Get Editor V1 free (works with free models): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
The edit at the start of this video cost me $0. No editor, no Claude, no ChatGPT: a free open model (GLM 5.3 Flash in OpenCode) made it with my Editor V1 skill and a one-line prompt 👇

🤝 Stuck installing? We run weekly calls in the Skool to help you.
Not sponsored by OpenCode or Z.ai (GLM). Nobody paid me for this.

💸 What $0 means
No Claude subscription, no ChatGPT, no credits, no API key, no account, no card. OpenCode's own counter for the session: 1.6 million tokens, $0.00. GLM 5.3 Flash is free in OpenCode "for a limited time". After that it's $0.15 in / $0.50 out per 1M tokens.

🧠 Why it wasn't possible a week ago
For AI to edit a video you need an agent that opens your files, runs tools and keeps working for an hour without you. That meant Claude Code and at least the $20 Claude plan. Free models were too small, or got lost on a long job. 3 things changed:
1. OpenCode: a free, open-source agent like Claude Code. It reads the same skill folders, so my Claude skills work as they are.
2. A big free model inside it: since Oct 16, GLM 5.3 Flash is free in OpenCode. 321 billion parameters, MIT license, 6M+ downloads on Hugging Face last month. It runs on OpenCode's servers, so a weak computer is fine.
3. The skill: Editor V1 holds my whole editing system (pace, colors, sounds, captions, the rules it can't break). The model just follows the recipe. No massive prompt.

💻 What ran where
Cutting, graphics, rendering and the sound mix ran on my MacBook Air (16 GB). Only the model ran on OpenCode's servers: 321B parameters don't fit on a laptop. Qwen 3.5 (9B) already runs on mine for carousels, but it's too small to edit. For now.

🎬 Which of my skills work with a free model
✅ Editor V1 (the edit you just saw)
✅ My screen-share editor (tested)
🟡 My short-form editor: should work, not tested in OpenCode yet
❌ My motion graphics skill: too much heavy code for open models right now
Tip: build skills with Claude (it's much smarter), then run them with the free model. As good as Opus 5.5? No. But it does the work.

📥 How to install (step by step)
Mac or Windows. On Windows, OpenCode recommends WSL (Linux inside Windows): https://opencode.ai/docs/windows-wsl
1. Install OpenCode. On Mac press Cmd + Space, type Terminal, open it, paste this line and hit enter (the exact line I tested):
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
2. In my Skool, open the Editor V1 post, open the Google Drive and download the Editor V1 zip. Leave it in Downloads. Don't move it, don't unzip it.
3. Close the terminal, open a new one, type opencode and hit enter. No sign-in. If you see "connect", skip it (that's for paid models).
4. Type /models, search "free", pick GLM 5.3 Flash Free. Press Ctrl + T until you see max.
5. Copy the setup prompt from the Google Drive, paste it into OpenCode, hit enter. It says "Claude Code" inside, that's fine: OpenCode reads the same folder. It installs the skill and the free tools (FFmpeg, Python, the video renderer, the speech model), asks before anything that needs your password, and asks if you want the cut-out effect (about 1 GB). Then it makes a 7-second test video. If you see it, you're done.
6. Type /new to start a fresh session.
7. Drag in your video and type: edit this video with editor v1
When it's done, say "open it for me", watch it and give notes. The more notes, the better it gets.

💡 My tips
1. Start short. My test was 38 seconds, not a 20-minute video.
2. Give notes with timestamps: "at second 5", not "the second 5".
3. Before it starts, ask how long it will take.

🔒 About the OpenCode hack
On Oct 17, OpenCode said its hosted Console was breached and API keys saved there may have leaked. It says the open-source app wasn't affected. This setup uses no Console account and no API key.

✏️ Notes
• In the free model's edit, the graphics show the Opus 4.5 page while I say Opus 5.5. I left it as the model made it.
• I said I might be the first. Smaller tests exist (a Shorts-trimming skill, a paid model editing for $0.33), but I couldn't find a free open model doing a full edit from one line.

snippet.title: Claude Duet vs ChatGPT Dots vs GrokBot
snippet.description:
Grok Bot, Muse, Dots, and now Claude Duet. In 10 weeks, 4 of the biggest AI companies dropped an always-on agent. They all do the same basic thing, so I skipped the obvious and went straight to what's different: 8 categories, a winner for each, and a final leaderboard. At the end, a free skill that puts the best feature of all 3 inside Claude Code 👇

🎁 Get Show It Once (and all my other skills) free in my Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
🤝 Stuck installing? We run weekly calls in the Skool to help you.

⚠️ Duet is on a waitlist and I don't have access yet, so everything on Duet comes from what Anthropic published, not my own test. Not sponsored.

🏆 The 8 categories
1. Price: Duet. Included in Claude Pro ($20/month). Grok Bot starts at $30 (Premium on The X Subscription), Dots at ChatGPT Pro ($100). Catch: Duet is waitlist only, and Grok Bot is the only one where I found a free trial.
2. Usage: Dots. Talking to your dot doesn't count toward your ChatGPT limits, and in its first month Dots usage doesn't count at all. Duet shares your Claude limits and checks your apps every few hours to save them. Grok Bot's weekly allowance is shared with Grok and Cursor, the number isn't published, and people say it runs out fast.
3. Who can use it today: Grok Bot. No waitlist, no country block I could find. Dots on Pro isn't in the EU, UK or Switzerland (you need Business with a Premium seat). Duet: US only, Pro and Max, waitlist.
4. Number of agents: Grok Bot. 50+ bots in group chats that hand work off. Dots and Duet: 1 each, for now.
5. Apps: Duet, on paper. 6,000+ connectors and plugins, and it can buy things with a virtual card. Dots: 4,000+. Grok Bot: no number, but it uses the computer when there's no connector.
6. Your work day: Dots. Slack, Teams, @dot in comments, you can call it, and it starts work in Codex. Grok Bot lives on X with its own email per bot. Duet lives in its own app.
7. Safety: Duet, on paper. It never sees your passwords, blocks sharing card numbers and IDs, and some things (trading stocks, moving money) are off-limits even with your approval. Dots is close: auto-review, Custom Rules, Activity View. Grok Bot checks before anything it can't undo, but the full action log is Enterprise only.
8. Learning by watching: Grok Bot, the only one. Record a task (up to 10 min) and it turns it into a skill. Dots and Duet can't do that.

Bonus: Duet runs on Opus 5.5, Dots on GPT-6 Astra. Grok Bot has no model picker, and its help page mentions Opus 5.5. So sometimes your Grok Bot is running on Claude.

📊 Leaderboard
Grok Bot: 3 wins (access, agents, learning by watching)
Duet: 3 wins (price, apps, safety), all on paper
Dots: 2 wins (usage, work day)
Want one today? Grok Bot. Team on Slack or Teams with Pro? Your dot. In the US on Claude Pro or Max? Join the Duet waitlist.

🎥 Show It Once (free skill)
Grok Bot's teach feature doesn't record your voice: it sees what you clicked, not why. So I built it for Claude Code. Record your screen doing a boring task and talk while you do it, then say "learn this". It grabs every screen that changes plus what you said, plays the steps back, asks 3 questions max and writes a skill. If there's a faster way (an app you connected, a direct download), it uses that, then runs it once while you watch. Schedule it on your computer (has to be awake) or in the cloud (connected apps only). It asks before it sends, posts, pays or deletes anything.

📥 How to install
1. Join my free Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
2. Open the Show It Once post and download the folder
3. Open Claude Code, paste the install prompt, hit enter
4. New session, say "learn this" with your recording

✏️ Corrections
• At launch, Grok Bot needed a $200 to $300/month plan (Cursor Ultra or SuperGrok Heavy). Its free trial is still offered today.
• Scheduled on your computer, the skill works with your files. Claude's docs don't confirm browser use on a schedule.

snippet.description:
🔗 Try Higgsfield: https://higgsfield.ai/s/video-model-showdown-kling-4-jadm-h-cJsSBE

Raw take on the left, the same take edited by Claude on the right. I didn't edit a single frame: every picture, every color, every sound. None of the pictures are AI generated. They're real, and Claude found them online on its own. I turned it into a free Claude skill called Editor V1 👇

🎁 Get Editor V1 (and all my other skills) free in my Skool: 

https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790/classroom/2a43afcd?md=725e5006df2f41a0a597d560b5bb5ae3

🤝 Stuck installing? My business partner and I run bi-weekly calls to help you.

🛠️ How I built it
I gave Claude Opus 5.5 three reels with the edits I wanted (real pictures, colors changing, super fast, a sound on everything) and told it to study them frame by frame. It went through all 5,982 frames and measured:
• how often the picture changes (in one reel, 175 times a minute)
• the colors, where the captions sit, how big the words get
• the sound effects on their own (it split the voice from the music)
Then it turned it all into one named style. Now I just say "use Editor V1".

❌ Version 1 was bad
My notes: use the sounds I gave you, more imagination, more clips, look at the 3 reels to the millisecond. It went deeper and found stuff I never noticed:
• at least half of every reel is moving clips, not still pictures
• a lot of lines are puns (I said "leaked", it showed a dripping tap)
• most shots slowly zoom in, and every new shot starts blurry and goes sharp
• a picture on screen for 4 seconds counts as a mistake
Version 2 was way better. First message to that demo: about 1 hour 15 minutes, studying the reels included.

⚙️ How it works
Claude isn't a video model here, it writes code. HyperFrames (free, open source) plays that code like a web page and renders it frame by frame into an MP4 on your Mac, so changing one thing only changes that thing. It writes down where every picture comes from with its licence, and checks the facts while it looks.

💰 What it costs
Almost $0: just your Claude subscription. HyperFrames is free, transcription runs on your Mac, music is your own (no copyright) or made with ACE-Step 1.5, and the pictures are public domain or Creative Commons.

🎬 AI vs a real editor
A real editor will always get more detail. But if the news drops this morning and your video comes out 3 days later, it's over. Would I pay an editor today? Yes, one who uses AI.

📏 Long form & short form
Short form: go bananas. Long form: full speed in the hook and at each chapter start, then shots breathe 1 to 2 seconds. My face is one more picture in the stream, about a third of the time.

👥 Who it's for
• News, founder stories, companies, products, history: anything about real things
• Businesses that want their videos to feel like a documentary
• Editors with clients: it saves you hours

📥 How to install
1. Join my free Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
2. Open the Editor V1 post, download the folder from Google Drive
3. Open Claude Code, paste the install prompt from the folder, hit enter
4. New session, type /model, pick Opus 5.5 (don't go cheap on the model)
5. Give it your video and say "use the style Editor V1"

🎨 Make your own style
Pick 2 or 3 videos (not more), have Claude study them frame by frame, let it make a demo from one of your old videos, be honest about what you don't like, then name the style.

snippet.title: I Ranked Every AI Video Model (FREE Prompts)
snippet.description:
🔗 Try Higgsfield: https://higgsfield.ai/s/video-model-showdown-kling-4-jadm-h-cJsSBE 
📚 All the prompts that I have used: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Ti8BvnXb6GoBGyq5uCVbkQdpXDjXUW0a?usp=sharing

Same prompt, 8 AI video models on Higgsfield, plus the brand-new Kling 4.0. Which one would you pick blind? 

I ran the same prompt AI test through Seedance 2.5, Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, MiniMax H3, Wan 3.0, Grok Imagine 1.5, FLUX 3 and Gemini Omni 1.1, every one on Higgsfield AI with the exact same prompt and the exact same settings. No rewriting, no prompt enhancer, one try each. You watch every result blind, then we go through the chart: what each model got right, what it got wrong, and what it cost in credits.

This video is sponsored by Higgsfield.

🎬 What is Higgsfield?
Higgsfield puts the top AI video models in one place. You write your prompt once, pick a model from one selector, and switching to the next one is a single click. Add your own reference images, pick the length, ratio and quality, and you see the credit price on the Generate button before you spend anything. Text to video AI and reference images in the same workflow, so you can run an AI video model comparison like this one yourself.

So here's my challenge: paste the same prompts, pick your own winner, and tell me in the comments if you agree with me 👇
▶ Try every model on Higgsfield: https://higgsfield.ai/s/video-model-showdown-kling-4-jadm-h-cJsSBE


⚡ What about Kling 4.0?
Kling 4.0 just came out and it isn't on Higgsfield yet (it's coming soon), so I ran it on Kling's own site with the same prompts, the same settings and the same reference images. It plays blind with the others, and at the end of every round you see it next to Kling 3.0. Its prices are Kling credits, not Higgsfield credits.

🥊 The 3 rounds
1. Cleopatra in the desert: she backs a white sports car out of a truck by the pyramids, the exhaust shoots flames and she drifts off, all in one phone shot. 12 seconds, cheapest settings, and every model got the same 4 reference images.
2. A home video from 2003: a girl in Seoul feeds a stray cat, hangs her laundry and says hello to her neighbour in Korean. 7 moments in 15 seconds, highest quality.
3. Tiny people: a girl a fifth of normal size does parkour through a shop, then 2 lines of text on screen. Cheapest settings.

💳 What it cost (Higgsfield credits, all 8 models)
• Cleopatra: 235
• Home video: 825
• Tiny people: 367.5 (includes Seedance 2.5's first try)
Kling 4.0 on kling.ai: 108 + 202 + 135 Kling credits.

🏆 My picks (you're the judge though)
There's no single best AI video generator for everything, so here's how I'd pick:
• Seedance 2.5 if you have the budget. For that old camcorder look, try it at 480p instead of 1080p.
• MiniMax H3 if you want the most for your credits.
• FLUX 3 for the old film look.
• Gemini Omni 1.1 if you only need 10 seconds.
• Kling 4.0 is a real jump from Kling 3.0: it did every moment and spelled the text right.

📝 Fair-test notes
• Gemini Omni 1.1 can only make 10 seconds, so it got 10 instead of 15 (or 12 in the Cleopatra round).
• MiniMax H3 only renders at 2K on Higgsfield, so sharpness isn't judged.
• Cheapest settings = mostly 480p. FLUX 3's and Kling 4.0's minimum is 720p.
• The Cleopatra prompt is a shortened version so it fits every model's prompt limit. Earlier tests with the long version aren't part of the comparison.
• In the tiny people round, my first Seedance 2.5 try put real candy brands on the packaging. I made the no-brand part stronger for every model and gave Seedance 2.5 a second try (both tries are counted). Clips with real-looking brands are blurred.

📂 Every result + the prompts (and the hotel ad prompt I mentioned at the end) are in my free Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
