snippet.title: Claude Video Editing. Posting is Now on EASY MODE. (Turned It Into A Skill)
snippet.description:
How I posted 197 reels and TikToks, 3 to 7 a day, with only 20 minutes of recording. 5 AI systems in Claude Code do the rest: one finds the news, one writes the script, one edits the video, one makes the thumbnail, and one posts it with Blotato. I turned all 5 into one free skill 👇

🎁 The full system is free in my Skool, in the post for this video: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Stuck installing it? We run free weekly calls in the Skool to help you set it up.

⚡ The Higgsfield offer I mentioned for the covers (no subscription needed, you can also use their API and pay as you go): https://higgsfield.ai/s/video-model-showdown-kling-4-jadm-h-cJsSBE

🧠 The 5 systems
1. The news (my scraper): it asks who you are, what you do and who you're talking to, then scrapes your niche and gives you a list of content ideas. You pick the ones you like. A dentist gets the taboo topics, the most common surgeries, the most common teeth problems. For me (AI), it goes through GitHub, Reddit, YouTube and the AI companies' blogs.
2. The script: a catchy hook, value spread through the whole video (not all in the first seconds), and a call to action at the end. It learns how you talk from your recordings, refines every line that doesn't sound like you, and never uses the words on your blacklist. It wrote me 213 scripts between Aug 16 and Sep 28.
3. The editor (short form, 9:16): cuts mistakes, restarts and long pauses, cuts you out of the background, puts the real posts and pages on screen, word-by-word captions, color grading, 25 to 40 sound effects. 5 styles and a 21-rule blacklist (no emojis, never 2 highlights at once). Every note you give it gets saved.
4. The thumbnail (reel cover): one world + one scale trick + the same text style every time, with the words straight from the script. Me on every cover with my AI character on Higgsfield, 3 to 4 versions, I pick one. It uses Higgsfield credits.
5. Posting: Blotato connected inside Claude. Claude writes the caption and hashtags, Blotato posts to Instagram, TikTok and Facebook at the times I pick. Nothing goes out without my OK.

⚙️ How to install it
1. Skool → the post for this video → Google Drive → download the zip
2. Open Claude Code in that folder
3. Copy the install prompt, paste it into Claude Code, hit enter
4. In Claude: Settings → Connectors → add Blotato (and Higgsfield if you want your own character on the covers)
5. Start a new session, answer the questions (who you are, what you do, who you're talking to), then say "scrape for me"
Use Opus 5.5 (type /model in Claude Code). It's a big job, don't go cheap on the model.

💡 My 5 tips
1. Start with 1 video a day, then ramp up
2. Record everything in one go
3. Messed up a line? Just say it again, the editor cuts it
4. Don't like something? Tell Claude, and it updates the skill
5. Understand your script and where to put the emphasis, don't just read it off a teleprompter

✏️ To be precise
• 0:00 "197": that's the post count on my Instagram (build.withjade), so it can include a few carousels, not only reels.
• 2:21 "GitHub, Reddit, X…": in my own runs the X source didn't work (the free proxy quota was used up in all 14 saved briefs), so my ideas came from GitHub, Reddit, Hacker News, YouTube and the AI blogs. A free Jina key turns X on.
• 5:33 "30 to 40 minutes" per short: that's the editing. With my own review, it's closer to an hour.
• 10:07 "not seven, not 16": 16 is the most scripts the system wrote in one day (Sep 21), not posts.

I made 3 faceless videos with Claude: a 3-minute survival story, a 33-second horror short and a 30-second 3D history explainer. No image generator, no video model, no stock footage. 1. Start from a faceless format that's already getting views. Take the format (pacing, layout, how the narrator talks), never the story or the characters.
2. Make a style sheet: 1 image with all the rules of your world (fonts, colors with hex codes, characters, props, the world, frame layout, rules). I made mine in Higgsfield with GPT Image 2.0.

snippet.title: What Is The Best Model For Motion Graphics (Tested)
snippet.description:
✅Higgsfield Promo: https://higgsfield.ai/s/katana-inside-claude-yt-jadm-h-xUOkwW

Which AI is the best at motion graphics? I gave Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-6 Astra the exact same job: the first 30 seconds of a music video. Same song, same lyrics, same shot list, same images, same prompt. I show you what each one made, how long it took and what it cost. You're the judge 👇

🎁 Free skills every week in my Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Stuck setting one up? We now run free weekly calls in the Skool to help you.

🧪 The setup (the same for all 3)
• Song: made locally with ACE-Step, $0
• Images and clips: Nano Banana, Kling and Higgsfield
• Rendered with HyperFrames (open source) on my Mac
• The same prompt word for word, the same shot list, the same skills
• Each model did the design, effects, code, self-checks and final render on its own. The only message I sent was the same "keep going" when the tool paused.

⚖️ Fair is fair
• Gemini ran through OpenRouter, but inside opencode (a coding agent like Claude Code), not a chat window. It had the whole project folder and the same tools Opus had: read and write files, run commands, render, look at its own frames, use helper agents.
• GPT-6 Astra had the same setup inside Codex, OpenAI's own tool.
• Opus built its version last week in Claude Code, and it had a 15-second test round that I reviewed. Gemini and GPT got 1 prompt, no feedback.
• The song literally says "Opus five point five", and Gemini named its terminal window "Claude Opus 5.5".

📊 The numbers
Gemini 4 Argon: about 63 minutes, 179 model calls, $9.87 paid on OpenRouter (about $1.60 of that was lost to a bug in opencode, not Gemini). That's Argon's launch price; it's set to double later.
GPT-6 Astra: about 23 minutes of work, 116 calls. It ran on ChatGPT Plus ($20/month), hit the Plus limit halfway, and I paid $5.61 on OpenRouter to finish.
Claude Opus 5.5: about 1 h 15 min for the final build (4 helpers building 4 scenes at the same time), plus a 50-minute test round. About 544 calls. It ran on Claude Max ($200/month), so $0 on top: about 5% of my weekly limit, roughly $2.30 of the plan.

✏️ Corrections
• 2:17 I say "50 second test round". It was a 15-second test round (it took about 50 minutes).
• 4:24 and 6:12 I say GPT cost "around $11". That's what the Plus half would have cost at API prices. What I actually paid on top of my Plus plan was $5.61.
• 7:11 I say Argon's lava lamp cost "80 cents". It was 18 cents.

🐦 The side-by-side videos from X (all launch-day tests)
Gummy bears, Opus 5.5 vs Argon (Opus $7.20, Gemini $22): https://x.com/semichenkko/status/2110131790136401989

Gemini 4 Argon is officially out, and X is calling it the Opus killer. So I skipped Google's own charts, went straight to the independent benchmarks, and gave Argon and Claude Opus 5.5 the exact same app prompt to see which one builds the better app 👇

🐦 What people on X are saying
• The hype: someone who says they work at Google DeepMind: "I don't reach for Opus anymore"
• The other side: "Opus 5.5 is still the best model in the world"
• The skeptic: Google's launch charts for Gemini 3.1 Pro also "destroyed" Claude

• Alan Wake 2 converted to run natively on a Mac (Max Weinbach)
• A 3D museum of Apple computers, built without a single image given (Justine Moore)

⚔️ Side-by-side tests (read the label, not just the caption)
• Argon vs "Opus 5.5 Medium": Opus wasn't on its top setting
• "Argon: 3 min, 50 cents" comes from a company that sells access to Argon
• Another test found the opposite: Argon cost $5.29 vs about $1.50 for Opus
• Devin says Argon is the best Gemini on their leaderboard, but Opus 5.5 is above it on their own chart

📊 Independent benchmarks (Oct 13, 2026)
• Arena, blind human votes, text: Argon #1, Opus 5.5 #2
• WebDev Arena: Opus 5.5 #1, Argon #9
• Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: Opus 5.5 58, Argon 53
• Hallucination rate (AA-Omniscience): Argon 15%, Opus 5.5 59%
• Vals Index: Argon #1 · Vals Terminal-Bench 4.0: Opus 5.5 #1, Argon #6

🧪 My test: Argon vs Opus 5.5
Same prompt, word for word: a phone app for a painting and flooring contractor. Scan the room, build it in 3D, change the paint and floor live, and price it into a quote the customer signs with their finger. One HTML file, no server. The sample room has exactly 1 correct price: $3,104.68.
✅ Both got the price right: $3,104.68
✅ Both built a working 3D room that updates the paint and floor live
💭 In my opinion, Opus 5.5 built the better app (its 3D room is more detailed). Judge for yourself.
To be fair: Opus 5.5 built its app in Claude Code, where it can run and check its own code. Argon built its app in a single API reply (high reasoning, about 7 minutes, $0.58). The camera scan wasn't tested on a real phone here.

💵 Price and who can use it
$2 per million input tokens, $10 output, until November 30, 2026. After that, $4 / $20, the same as Opus 5.5.
Google AI Pro and Ultra (Gemini app, AI Mode in Search), Ultra in Antigravity, and the paid Gemini API. Not on the free plan yet.

💭 My take
Argon is the real deal. For research, writing, legal or finance, I'd 100% try it, especially at half price. For coding and building skills, my choice comes down to tests like this one.

snippet.title: The 3 Levels Of Viral Carousels 0$ (Turned it into a skill)
snippet.description:
Higgsfield Promo: https://higgsfield.ai/katana?utm_source=yt&utm_medium=social&utm_category=gr&utm_campaign=Katana_inside_Claude_YT&utm_creator=jadm.h&utm_content_type=de&utm_post=xUOkwW&invite_code=katana-inside-claude-yt-jadm-h-xUOkwW

This is a $0 carousel. This is a $100 carousel. And this is a $1,000 carousel. The crazy part: the $100 one cost me $0. No API, no credits. And the $1,000 one isn't really a carousel, it's a system businesses pay for. Here's how each one is made, what it really costs, and which one you should be making 👇

🎁 Everything for the $100 carousel is free in my Skool: the skill, the style sheets and the exact prompt I used in this video
👉 https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Stuck installing a skill? We now run weekly calls in the Skool to help you set it up.

📊 Why carousels?
• Buffer compared every format on Instagram: carousels got a 6.9% engagement rate, Reels got 3.3%. More than double.
• Reels still get a bit more reach, but carousels are what people stop and interact with.
• If someone scrolls past your carousel, Instagram can show it to them again later, starting on slide 2. A Reel doesn't get that second chance.

💸 The price tag is what it looks like, not what you pay.

🟢 $0: Canva
Pick a template, change the color, type, export. Fast, free, and fine for a quick post. The problem: the template made every decision for you, so your post looks like 50 others. Typing "make it modern" into ChatGPT is worse: purple gradients, glowing brains, a new font on every slide.

🔵 $100 (that costs $0)
Way 1: Muse, Meta's app. Free tier (with a usage limit). Drag in 2 images, paste the prompt, and you can set it to make a new carousel every day. Not in every country yet.
Way 2: Qwen 3.5 9B from Alibaba, running locally in Ollama on my base MacBook Air (16 GB). About a 7 GB download, it can see images, and nobody counts your tokens.

The model isn't the secret. What you give it is:
1. A style sheet: 1 image with the colors (hex codes), the fonts and the rules
2. An example: a finished carousel in that same style
3. The prompt: a full page, not 1 line. Research from official sources, a link for every number, show the plan first, and a checklist at the end so it checks its own work
It writes the carousel as a web page, so the text is real, sharp and spelled right. Open it in your browser and screenshot each slide.
Test 1: a 3-slide carousel about Claude Haiku 5.5. Test 2: a carousel built around my own photo.
The limits: a 9B model is not Opus. It's slower, and sometimes you have to ask it twice.

🟣 $1,000: motion graphics, as a system
Every slide moves, synced to music. It's built for agencies, because a business doesn't want 1 carousel. It wants posts going out every week without touching anything. So you're selling an automation:
1. Claude Opus 5.5 finds the niche
2. It finds the ideas that are working in that niche right now
3. It writes the hook, every slide and the CTA
4. Higgsfield (connected inside Claude) makes the images with GPT Image 2.5: the product, the scene, or an avatar like Jad-me
5. It brings it to life: real motion design written in code, not an AI video
6. Blotato posts it every week
What it costs: a Claude plan, Higgsfield credits and a Blotato plan. It doesn't cost $1,000. That's what you could sell it for.
Most of the pieces are already in my Skool (the motion carousel skill, the avatar part, the style sheets), and I'm turning the full system into a skill too.

snippet.title: Muse Wonder vs Opus 5.5
snippet.description:
Higgsfield Promo: https://higgsfield.ai/s/katana-inside-claude-yt-jadm-h-xUOkwW

Meta just released Muse Wonder, their first real frontier model. I read Meta's own benchmark chart and checked it against independent scores, and the model you can actually buy is not the one that looks best on the chart. Here's what it is, what it costs, and whether you should switch from Claude 👇

🧠 What Muse Wonder is
• 2 models: Muse Wonder (Meta Model API + Muse Code) and Muse Wonder Full (Muse Code subscribers only, not on the API)
• Meta's first frontier model since Alexandr Wang took over Meta's AI
• Active memory: remembers what matters to you over days, weeks and months
• Active focus: trained not to give up when it hits a blocker
• Text, image, video and audio in, text out, 1M token context

🎬 Meta's demos (Meta says they were shortened)
• Plans a Saturday run from your calendar and health app, then maps the route
• Designs a birthday T-shirt for Coco the cat from Instagram photos, then orders it
• Finds the error on an urgent care bill and emails the insurance for you
• Builds a wedding seating chart from a guest list full of notes

💵 The price
$4 per million input tokens, $20 output. Exactly the same as Claude Opus 5.5. And it's closed: no open weights like Llama.

📊 Meta's own chart (14 benchmarks)
✅ Wins: legal work (10.0 vs Opus 4.2), memory (85.6 vs 81.5), long coding (DeepSWE 78.8 vs 74.2)
❌ Opus 5.5 still has the top score on 6 of the 14 rows, the same as Wonder Full
❌ The Muse Wonder you can buy beats Opus on only 5 of 14
⚠️ The memory test and the "Personal Superintelligence Index" are Meta's own internal benchmarks, and Meta says its competitor runs are "best-effort"

🔎 Independent scores (Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index)
Claude Opus 5.5: 58 (#1)
Muse Wonder Full: 56
Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra: 53
Muse Wonder: 52 (#9 of 219)
Fair is fair: Muse Wonder costs $4.52 per task vs $5.98 for Opus, because it uses half the tokens. Opus is faster.

💭 My take
Meta is back, and memory is the right bet. But for coding, editing my videos and building skills, I'm staying on Claude: same price, higher independent score.

🎁 Get both editing skills free in my Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

🙅 Not sponsored. I don't make money from my channel or the skills. The only thing you pay for is your Claude subscription.

💬 I read all your comments
Your #1 question: "How do you edit your videos?" Claude edited this whole video: the layouts, the motion graphics and the real screenshots. I have 2 AI editors: long form (this video) and short form (one of my shorts did over 100K views on TikTok). They're why I could post 16 videos in 16 days (over 300,000 views). A month ago I posted once or twice a week.

🤔 Why an AI editor?
An edit isn't one job, it's 7. If a human edit comes back days later, AI news is already old. These skills do all 7 for $0 on top of your Claude subscription.

👥 Who it's for
• Businesses that need content every week (YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels)
• Brands: same colors, fonts and feel in every video
• Personal brands that want to post a lot and stay consistent
• Marketers: every client gets their own style
• Agencies: offer it as part of your service

⚙️ How it works: the 7 jobs
Claude can't watch or make a video. It reads and writes text and uses free tools on your computer. Drop your recording in the folder, say "edit this", pick a style.
1️⃣ Transcribe: every word with its exact time, using Parakeet (free, runs on my laptop). It once dropped 13 seconds of audio, so the editor now checks the transcript minute by minute.
2️⃣ Cut: pauses, ums and retakes. Say a line twice and it keeps the good one.
3️⃣ Research: every site, tool or post I name, it opens Chrome and screenshots the real thing.
4️⃣ Motion graphics: no video model. Every chart and title is a little web page. HyperFrames screenshots every frame and FFmpeg glues them together, so everything stays editable.
5️⃣ Color: grades the footage against the reference and can cut me out so big words go behind my head.
6️⃣ Sound (mostly for shorts): every layout change gets a transition and a sound.
7️⃣ Finish: joins the chapters, writes captions and timestamps. It never posts. It renders and stops so I watch first.

🎨 Styles and rules
"Edit my video" alone gives you the default look everyone has. That's AI slop. Every style I have came from a video I loved: Claude grabs frames with FFmpeg and measures the colors, fonts, layouts and timing. This style changes layout every 8 seconds. Long form has 8 styles, short form has 5.
Rules: I give notes like a director, then say "add that to your skill". My short-form editor has a blacklist of 21 rules, each from a cut I rejected. You start with all my notes.

🎬 A real edit
It transcribes, cuts, writes a plan (every chapter, what goes on screen) and waits for my OK.

💰 What it costs
I'm on Claude Max. No paid APIs: Parakeet, HyperFrames and FFmpeg are all $0. Building the skills cost me over $200 (I maxed out my plan), and that part is done for you. I've edited 81 shorts with it, 5 in one day.

📥 How to install
1. Join my free Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
2. Find the post for this video. It links to my Google Drive. Download both editors (long + short), each in its own folder.
3. Open Claude Code, open the install prompt, copy everything, paste it in and hit enter. It sets up the free tools for you.
4. Start a new Claude Code session so the skill loads, drop your recording in and say "edit this".
5. Use Opus 5.5 (type /model). Editing is a big job, so don't go cheap on the model.

⚠️ It's not perfect
Your first edit won't be perfect. Mine weren't. Give it notes and say "add it to the skill". The voice jumps some of you noticed? That's my own manual cutting. Someone still has to decide what's good, so editing experience gets you even better results.

🎁 Get the free music video skill: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

🙅 Not sponsored. I don't make money from the skill and I'm not monetized. Everything here came out of my own pocket.

👀 How the viral ones were really made
1️⃣ The original (2.8M views) was posted by a Berkeley master's student with about 1,600 followers. Claude ran 7 Opus 5.5 agents, each coding a scene at the same time.
2️⃣ Donald's remake (almost 4M views) says "one prompt" and "Claude worked for 12 hours". His prompt is 9,608 characters, tells Claude to spend all his Max plan usage, and gives it roughly $2,000 in AI credits (Seedance 2.5, ElevenLabs). Frame by frame: 114 cuts in 2:21, and most of it is motion graphics, not AI video.
3️⃣ The Blender one: Opus 5.5 wrote the code, but the girl, key images and music came from paid models (MiniMax, Midjourney).

🎬 How Claude makes a video
Claude can't output video. It writes code (a web page), a browser screenshots every frame, and FFmpeg (free) glues them together. 2:45 at 30 fps = 4,950 screenshots. Because it's code, you can change anything and render again.

🎵 Step 1: the song ($0)
Claude wrote the lyrics and made the song on my MacBook Air (16 GB) with ACE-Step 1.5, a free, open-source music model. No Suno, no subscription. It made 4 takes, transcribed each one and picked the clearest. The singer kept saying Claude wrong, so Claude spelled its name "Clawd" in the lyrics. Then it timed every word.

💰 Version 1: paid
• Her character sheet: Higgsfield, 10 credits
• 21 poses (Nano Banana 2.1) + 6 clips of her moving, 5 s each (Kling 3.0), through kie.ai (pay as you go, no subscription)
• A lip-sync test ($0.24). It worked, but it looked like every AI avatar, so I dropped it and told Claude: make her out of code.
• 17 scenes, 15 builders coding at the same time. Then Claude watched it and fixed what was wrong.
Total: $2.97 on kie.ai + 10 Higgsfield credits. Not $2,000.

🆓 Version 2: $0
One rule: nothing paid. No Higgsfield, no kie.ai, no AI images, no AI video. Only my Claude subscription.
• Code can't draw an anime girl yet, so Claude made its own mascot: CURSOR.
• He sings with no lip-sync model. His mouth follows the vowels measured from the song itself.
• The rulebook: nothing stays still for more than 0.4 s, something hits on every beat, everything bright.
• Claude grades itself: it puts a screenshot of every shot on one page, caught the galaxy turning into a white blob, and fixed it.

📊 Paid vs $0
• Character: paid wins if you want a real character or your own avatar. A few credits is enough, then code does the rest. My take: a mix of both.
• Money: $2.97 + 10 Higgsfield credits vs $0.
• Claude usage (Max plan, weekly limit): paid about 16-19%, $0 about 19%. $0 saves you money, not usage.
• Time: each one took Claude about 1.5 to 2 hours. Not 12.
• Just starting? Use the $0 one and ask for 15 seconds first.

⚙️ How to install the skill
1. Join my free Skool: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
2. Find the post with this video's title (or go to the free resources). It links to my Google Drive. Download the folder.
3. Open Claude Code, open the install prompt from the Drive, copy everything, paste it in and hit enter. It sets up the free tools (ACE-Step, HyperFrames) for you.
4. Start a new Claude Code session so the skill loads.
5. Use Opus 5.5: type /model and pick it. These are big builds.
The music model takes about 11 GB of disk space. On Pro? Start with a 30-second video, not the full song.

snippet.title: I Tested Nano banana 2.1 vs GPT 2.5 (No Hype)
snippet.description:
Nano Banana 2.1 just came out, and Google says it's better across the board and cheaper. OpenAI says the same kind of thing about GPT Image 2.5 Flare. So I looked at their own charts, checked an independent leaderboard, and then ran both models through 8 real tests: realism, light, a complicated scene, text, my own AI character, editing a photo, removing people and fixing an old damaged photo. Same prompt, 1 try each, no re-rolls 👇

🙅 Not sponsored. I've had sponsor emails, but it's not right for me right now, and most of what those tools do can be done for free.

📈 What they claim
Google (Oct 6): Nano Banana 2.1 is better across the board: quality, text and keeping the same character. On Google's API it costs about half of the previous model (3.36¢ vs 6.70¢ per 1K image).
Google's own chart (Overall Preference): Nano Banana 2.1 scores 1050, Nano Banana 2 scores 990, Nano Banana Pro scores 935. Every model on that chart is a Google model. GPT isn't on it.
OpenAI (Sep 8): GPT Image 2.5 has more natural lighting and richer textures, keeps the people from your reference photos, follows edits more reliably over multiple turns, and cuts generation time by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0. It comes in 2 versions: Flare (the fast one, the one I tested) and Sunburst (slower, more detail).

🏆 What Arena says
Arena is a public leaderboard where people vote between 2 images without knowing which model made them (page from Oct 6).
Making images: #1 GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst (1425), #2 GPT Image 2.5 Flare (1398), #5 Nano Banana 2.1 (1328).
Editing images: #1 Sunburst, #2 Flare, #6 Nano Banana 2.1.
To be fair, Nano Banana 2.1 is brand new: about 5,000 votes so far vs about 16,000 for Flare, so it can still move.

🧪 How I tested
Everything ran on Higgsfield. Same prompt for both models, same settings (2K, medium quality), 1 try each, no re-rolls. What you see is exactly what came out.
Price on Higgsfield: Nano Banana 2.1 = 2 credits per image, GPT Image 2.5 Flare = 1 credit.

📊 The 8 tests
1️⃣ A real phone photo: GPT. It really looks like a friend took it with the flash on: blown-out faces, grainy background, motion blur. Nano Banana looks like a photographer lit it.
2️⃣ Light and detail: GPT, barely. GPT looks like a movie and you can see the lake and the church out the window, but the face is way too sharp. Nano Banana followed "no over-sharpening", but the window is just white. I went back and forth on this one.
3️⃣ A complicated scene (ramen stall in Tokyo): GPT, really close. Both menus and prices are right. GPT put the cook left of center and drew exactly 3 bowls. Nano Banana put the cook in the middle and drew 4.
4️⃣ Text: both got every word right, so the text itself is a tie. GPT gets the point because Nano Banana's tin stands on its edge like a wheel.
5️⃣ My character: GPT. I first gave it to Nano Banana, then looked again: GPT's version looks more like me.
6️⃣ Edit it, keep my face (leather jacket + night): tie. Both kept my face.
7️⃣ Remove the people: GPT. It filled the space with trees. Nano Banana turned the people into more rock and left a white lump.
8️⃣ Fix an old photo: GPT. Both fixed it, but GPT's looks more real and less like a filter.

Final score: GPT Image 2.5 Flare 7, tie 1, Nano Banana 2.1 0. And on Higgsfield, GPT is also half the price.

snippet.title: The 6 Levels of Viral Carousels 0$ Turned It Into a Skill ( For FREE )
snippet.description:
There are 6 levels of Instagram carousels, and most people are stuck on level 1 or 2. In this video I go through all 6, from the Canva template everyone uses to avatar carousels where every slide moves with music. For each one I show what it looks like, how it's made and what it costs, and I turned all of it into 1 free Claude skill 👇

🎁 Get the free carousel skill (installs in about 2 minutes): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

🪜 The 6 levels
1️⃣ Canva: same template as everyone else. Cover the username and you can't tell who made it.
2️⃣ Untrained AI: "make it modern and premium" with no reference. Purple gradients, glowing brains, robots shaking hands. It's slop, not because AI is bad, but because nobody told it what good looks like.
3️⃣ Trained: a style sheet + guardrails. $0, or a paid route if you want nicer images. If you only take 1 level from this video, take this one.
4️⃣ Avatar: your face, a mascot or your whole team in every post. I locked an AI version of me on Higgsfield and made 9 carousels with it.
5️⃣ Motion graphics: every slide is a looping video with its own music and sound effects. $0.
6️⃣ Avatar + motion graphics: your avatar carousel split into layers and brought to life. My favorite so far.

🎨 What's a style sheet? (level 3)
1 image with your whole design on it: your colors with the exact hex codes, your fonts, the pieces you reuse (a pill, a card), how each slide is laid out, and rules like "red is only ever a block, never text". Start from designs you actually like and ask yourself what you like about them. Typing "make it better" 10 times won't fix a carousel, and paying for better images won't either. The style sheet fixes it.

🧑 4 rules for avatar carousels (level 4)
1. Make a picture of the feeling, not the topic.
2. Borrow something people already know.
3. It has to work tiny. People see your cover at the size of a stamp: 1 big word, 1 clear image.
4. Keep the face consistent. With only a reference photo, the face slowly drifts, so use a style reference sheet of yourself too.

🎬 How the motion graphics work (levels 5 and 6)
Instagram lets you put videos inside a carousel. Claude can't make a video, it writes code: basically a web page that knows exactly what the screen looks like at every moment. A browser screenshots every frame and FFmpeg puts them together into an MP4. I use HyperFrames, a free open-source framework, for that. The music and sound effects are made with code too: no AI video model, no stock music, no credits. For level 6, every slide is split into layers (background, your cut-out, text, floating cards) so every piece can move on its own, starting from your original design.

💸 What it costs
Level 3 (free route) and level 5: $0. You only pay for your Claude subscription.
Level 3 (paid route): you pay per image, with Nano Banana Pro on kie.ai or Higgsfield's API, using your own key. It tells you how many credits it will use and waits for your "go".
Levels 4 and 6: the avatar images cost Higgsfield credits. The motion graphics part is still $0.

⚙️ How to install the skill
1. Go to my free Skool community and click the link. It opens a Google Drive.

snippet.title: New VIRAL Carousels With Motion Graphics 0$ Turned It Into a Skill (COPY ME)
snippet.description:
This is an Instagram carousel where every single slide moves. The ball, the text, the music, and every sound effect lands exactly on the beat. Claude made all of it, and the animation, music and sound effects cost me $0. I searched YouTube and couldn't find a single carousel where every slide is real motion design synced to music, so I built one and turned it into a free skill. Here are 2 examples, how motion design actually works, and the skill so you can make your own 👇

🎁 Get the free Live Carousel skill (the install prompt sets everything up in about 2 minutes): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

🎠 What's a live carousel?
Instagram lets you put videos inside a carousel. So instead of still images, every slide is a short looping video in Instagram size (1080x1350) with its own sound. People swipe, every slide moves, and the music keeps playing from one slide to the next, like 1 song.

🎬 The examples
1️⃣ No image at all: "Motion Design 101". 4 slides, cobalt blue, cream text and 1 orange ball that travels through the whole carousel. No photo, no image model, just design and code.
2️⃣ My own carousel, brought to life: the viral carousel my carousel generator skill made from 1 prompt. Claude rebuilt every slide in layers (background, my cut-out photo, text, title, floating cards), so every piece can move on its own. The song was made on my MacBook Air with ACE-Step 1.5, and each slide picks up the next bars of the same song.
➕ Bonus: a third one I made, right after example 2.

🧠 How motion design works
Motion design is graphic design that moves: text, shapes, logos, a ball, all designed with timing. Claude can't make a video directly. It writes code, basically a web page that knows exactly what the screen looks like at every moment. A browser takes a screenshot of every frame, and FFmpeg glues them together into an MP4. What makes it look good or cheap comes down to 3 rules: easing, weight and rhythm.

🥁 Why the beat matters
Everything runs at 120 BPM, so 1 beat every half second. Every hit, flip and bounce lands on a beat, and every slide is a whole number of bars. On Instagram a video slide loops, so if the music doesn't loop cleanly, you hear a jump every single time. Here you can't even tell where it starts.

🤖 Why not just use an AI video model?
You can send your carousel image to an AI video model and make it move. Sometimes it looks great, but you pay credits for every clip, you don't decide what moves or when, the text can melt or your face can change a little, and it has no idea what music to put in. Nothing here comes from a video model: the text stays razor sharp, every move lands on the beat, and if I don't like something, I change 1 line and render it again.

⚙️ How the skill works
Give it a topic or your own carousel images. It plans every slide (hook, rules, call to action), decides what moves, when and on which beat, makes the music and sound effects on your computer, and renders 1 MP4 per slide in Instagram size. It also makes a preview page so you can ask for quick changes. Then upload the videos as a carousel, in order, and you're done.

🤔 Which one should you use?
Teaching something, want a clean brand look, or don't have pictures? Go with example 1: pure motion design, nothing to generate, $0.
Already have images of you or your team? Go with example 2. You don't redesign anything, you just bring what you already have to life.

🔗 Tools I used (all free)
HyperFrames (the video framework): https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes
FFmpeg: https://ffmpeg.org
ACE-Step 1.5 (the song in example 2, runs on your computer): https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5
The skill makes its own music and sound effects with code, so you don't need to install ACE-Step to use it.

snippet.description:
I made 3 motion graphics videos with Claude: one from a simple prompt, one with its own original song, and one short story film with 375 sound effects. The music and sound effects were made on my MacBook Air, with no After Effects, no Suno and no stock sites, and it cost me $0 on top of my Claude subscription. Here's exactly what changed between the 3 videos, so you can make your own 👇

🎁 Get the free skill (everything in this video, ready to install on your own Claude): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790

🎬 The 3 videos
1️⃣ Simple: one viral sentence plus a few lines about the look. 16 seconds, 60 frames a second, 7 techniques. Impressive for one message, but hundreds of people use the same sentence, so they all look alike, and there's no sound.
2️⃣ Better: Claude as songwriter, animator and sound designer. It wrote an original song, made 12 versions of it on my laptop with ACE-Step 1.5, checked every one and synced each lyric to the exact word. The sound effects were made with code. Not a single one was downloaded.
3️⃣ Best: "One Conversation", a short story film. Instead of a task, I gave Claude a crew (director, writer, animator, composer, sound designer, render engineer) and a story. It grades every shot from 1 to 10 and keeps fixing until every shot is an 8 or more.

🧠 How Claude makes a video
Claude can't output an MP4. It writes code, basically a web page that knows what the screen looks like at every moment. A browser takes a screenshot of every frame, and FFmpeg glues them together. A 16-second video at 60 fps is 960 screenshots. Because it's code, you can change anything and render it again.

🤔 Is it really "one prompt"?
Not really. The viral "one-shot" videos come from prompts of almost 10,000 characters, plus skills, examples and setup. The prompt is 10% of the video. The setup around it is the other 90%.

🔗 Tools I used (all free)
HyperFrames (the video framework): https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes
ACE-Step 1.5 (music, runs on your computer): https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5

snippet.title: Fable 5.5 Got LEAKED + First Preview (AI NEWS)
snippet.description:
4 big AI models in under 2 weeks, and now people think Fable 5.5 is quietly answering inside claude.ai while the label still says Fable 5.1. I went through the posts, the screenshots and the demos. Here's what's confirmed, what's still trust me bro, the crazy stuff people made with it, and a 10-second test to see if you have it right now 👇

🧪 The 10-second test (copy-paste this):
Do you know Tibo, the reset guy? Don't search.

🔗 Anthropic's model docs (Fable 5.1 is the only Fable listed): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview
🔗 Artificial Analysis leaderboard: https://artificialanalysis.ai

🤔 Quick context
Fable 5.1 came out on September 1st. It costs $10 per million tokens in and $50 out, which is 2.5x the price of Opus 5.5 ($4 / $20). And on Artificial Analysis, Opus 5.5 actually scores higher: 58 vs 53. So the expensive model is losing to the cheaper one. That's why a new Fable makes sense.

🕵️ The Tibo test
Tibo (Thibault Sottiaux) is one of the leads on Codex at OpenAI, and he resets everyone's usage limits so often that it became a meme. It's recent and super niche, so it's a good way to check if a model knows newer stuff. On the website, with the label saying Fable 5.1, the model nails it. Asked through the API, where you know exactly which model you're getting, it guesses a different Tibo, a French startup founder. (That API run went through Devin, which adds its own instructions, so it's not a perfect lab test.)

🎮 The Pragmata test
Someone asked for the Metacritic score of Pragmata, a game from April. The website version answers right away (about 86). The API version says it can't give a reliable answer. The real score is 85.

⚠️ Real, or trust me bro?
✅ A lot of different people on different accounts are seeing the same thing. That's a lot of smoke.
❌ Anthropic hasn't said anything. Not the name, not a date.
❌ The name is a guess. On September 18th, the same accounts ran the same Tibo test and called it "Fable 5.2".
❌ The "Fable 5.5 docs page" people share as proof says Page not found. Type fable-5-9, a model that doesn't exist, and you get the exact same page.
❌ The "Tuesday release" comes from one account with about 10,000 followers, with no name and no source. To be fair, the Tuesday rumor for Opus 5.5 was right. But the same testing showed up 2 weeks ago and nothing launched.

🎨 What people made with it
1️⃣ Superman flying through 20 art styles in one continuous animation (@chetaslua)
2️⃣ 40,000 years of art history in 15 seconds (@cherry_mx_reds)
3️⃣ A full motion design reel from a single prompt (@Saccc_c)
4️⃣ The Grader, a 3.5-minute short film with 3D characters, voices and subtitles (@chetaslua)
5️⃣ The same floating Japanese garden prompt given to the new model and to Opus 5.5 on max in Claude Code (@vikktorrrre)
Remember, these are best-of demos from people who got lucky with the routing. We don't know how many tries they took, there are no benchmarks, and since the label always says 5.1, you can't be 100% sure which model made which demo.

✅ How to check if you have it
1. You need a paid plan, Pro or higher. Fable isn't on the free plan.
2. Go to claude.ai and pick Fable 5.1.
3. Turn off web search (or just keep "Don't search" in the prompt).
4. Type: Do you know Tibo, the reset guy? Don't search.
If it says Thibault Sottiaux, Codex, OpenAI and resetting limits, you're probably on the new one. If it guesses another Tibo, you're on the normal one.
You can't choose it. It's random, and it comes and goes. And Fable is one of the most expensive models, so it eats your usage fast. Don't spam it.

💭 My take
I think something new is really being tested. But if I'm paying for something, I want the label to say what I'm actually using. If you use it for real work in Claude Code and it suddenly behaves differently, you'd want to know why. When it's official, it's getting the same room quote test I gave Opus and Sol.

🧪 The 10-second test (copy-paste this):
Do you know Tibo, the reset guy? Don't search.

🔗 Anthropic's model docs (Fable 5.1 is the only Fable listed): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview
🔗 Artificial Analysis leaderboard: https://artificialanalysis.ai

🤔 Quick context
Fable 5.1 came out on September 1st. It costs $10 per million tokens in and $50 out, which is 2.5x the price of Opus 5.5 ($4 / $20). And on Artificial Analysis, Opus 5.5 actually scores higher: 58 vs 53. So the expensive model is losing to the cheaper one. That's why a new Fable makes sense.

🕵️ The Tibo test
Tibo (Thibault Sottiaux) is one of the leads on Codex at OpenAI, and he resets everyone's usage limits so often that it became a meme. It's recent and super niche, so it's a good way to check if a model knows newer stuff. On the website, with the label saying Fable 5.1, the model nails it. Asked through the API, where you know exactly which model you're getting, it guesses a different Tibo, a French startup founder. (That API run went through Devin, which adds its own instructions, so it's not a perfect lab test.)

🎮 The Pragmata test
Someone asked for the Metacritic score of Pragmata, a game from April. The website version answers right away (about 86). The API version says it can't give a reliable answer. The real score is 85.

⚠️ Real, or trust me bro?

❌ Anthropic hasn't said anything. Not the name, not a date.
❌ The name is a guess. On September 18th, the same accounts ran the same Tibo test and called it "Fable 5.2".
❌ The "Fable 5.5 docs page" people share as proof says Page not found. Type fable-5-9, a model that doesn't exist, and you get the exact same page.

Remember, these are best-of demos from people who got lucky with the routing. We don't know how many tries they took, there are no benchmarks, and since the label always says 5.1, you can't be 100% sure which model made which demo.

✅ How to check if you have it
1. You need a paid plan, Pro or higher. Fable isn't on the free plan.
2. Go to claude.ai and pick Fable 5.1.
3. Turn off web search (or just keep "Don't search" in the prompt).
4. Type: Do you know Tibo, the reset guy? Don't search.
If it says Thibault Sottiaux, Codex, OpenAI and resetting limits, you're probably on the new one. If it guesses another Tibo, you're on the normal one.
You can't choose it. It's random, and it comes and goes. And Fable is one of the most expensive models, so it eats your usage fast. Don't spam it.

💭 My take
I think something new is really being tested. But if I'm paying for something, I want the label to say what I'm actually using. If you use it for real work in Claude Code and it suddenly behaves differently, you'd want to know why. When it's official, it's getting the same room quote test I gave Opus and Sol.

snippet.title: Got Banned by OpenAI Twice Building His "Uncensored" AI (Open-source)
snippet.description:
PewDiePie just announced his own AI. It's called Ajax, it runs on your own computer, and it can handle your emails, your calendar and your web searches without anything leaving your device. It's not out yet, but here are 5 reasons I think it's worth keeping an eye on, explained simply. You don't need to be technical 👇

🔗 PewDiePie's Ajax page (check here to see when it comes out): https://data.pewdiepie.com
🔗 Odysseus on GitHub: https://github.com/odysseus-dev/odysseus

🤔 What is it?
There are 2 things. Odysseus is a free app PewDiePie started a few months ago. It puts an AI assistant on your own computer: chat, email, calendar, notes and research, all in one place. Ajax is the AI that runs inside it. Think of Odysseus as the house and Ajax as the assistant who lives there. He didn't build Ajax from scratch. He took Qwen, a free AI made by Alibaba, and trained it to do one job well.

5 reasons to keep an eye on it
1️⃣ Your stuff stays on your computer. Nothing gets sent to a company's servers, and he says his app doesn't collect any data.
2️⃣ It's small on purpose. Ajax is 9 billion parameters, more than 100x smaller than the big AIs are rumored to be. Small enough to run on your own computer.
3️⃣ It says no a lot less. He cut down the "Sorry, I can't help with that" answers, but he drew a line at anything that hurts other people or yourself.
4️⃣ People are paying attention. His Ajax video got almost 2 million views, and Odysseus has around 88,000 stars on GitHub.
5️⃣ It's still getting better. Ajax tries the same task 16 times, and the tries that work are used to teach it.

🚫 The OpenAI ban
One way to make a small AI smart is to train it on a bigger AI's answers. He used OpenAI's Sol, and OpenAI banned him. Twice.

⚠️ Real, or trust me bro?
He says it works about 9 out of 10 times, but that's his own number. Nobody else can test it yet because it's not out, and he took the countdown off his site (now it's coming "when it's ready"). Also, setting up Odysseus right now means typing commands into a terminal, so if you're not technical, this isn't something to download tonight.

✂️ Step 1: Cut
Claude transcribes your video word by word, then cuts out the pauses, the ums and the takes you messed up. Say a line twice and it keeps the last one.
✅ Whisper: free, but it runs on your own computer, so it's slow
✅ AssemblyAI: about $0.21 per hour of audio, super fast, with free hours when you sign up

🎨 Step 2: Animate
Tell Claude "animate my video" and you get the default look everybody has: same fonts, same gradients, same little icons. That's how AI slop happens. What you need is a design system, a rulebook for your style: your colors, your fonts, how much motion, how things come on screen. You don't need DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro for this.
How I build mine: I give Claude a video I love. It uses FFmpeg (free) to grab frames and turns the colors, the layout and the timing into a design system. That's how I built all 8 of my editing styles.

🎬 Step 3: Direct
Watch what Claude made like a director and give it notes. Then tell Claude to save your feedback into the skill, so the next video is already better. Every rule in my skill came from a note I gave once: no emojis on screen, every cut needs a sound, no random people as b-roll, show the real thing.

⚠️ Bonus tip: when your chat's context window hits about 40%, start a new chat. One video, one chat.

The week: Monday, Anthropic dropped Sonnet 5.5. Tuesday, OpenAI dropped GPT-6.1 Sol at DevDay. Wednesday, Google dropped Gemini 4 Argon. 3 days, 3 "best models in the world."

🔒 Can you use it?
Not yet. Google is only rolling Argon out to a small group of security testers (its Fairwind Program) for now, so I couldn't run my app test on it.

💰 Price per million tokens
Gemini 4 Argon: $2 in, $10 out (intro price, same as Sol), then $4 in, $20 out (same as Opus). Google hasn't said when the intro price ends
GPT-6.1 Sol: $2 in, $10 out
Claude Opus 5.5: $4 in, $20 out
✅ Argon can write up to 1 million tokens in one answer. Opus and Sol stop at 128,000

📊 Google's own chart
✅ Legal (Harvey): Argon 19.6%, Opus 3.8%
✅ Business automation (Zapier AutomationBench): Argon 51.3%, Opus 42.5%
⚠️ Loses 5 out of 19, mostly coding. Terminal coding (Terminal-Bench 4.0): Opus 66.4%, Argon 57.4%
⚠️ GPT-6.1 Sol isn't on the chart (it came out the day before)

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: Opus 5.5 57.6, Argon 52.6, Sol about 52
✅ Argon has the lowest hallucination rate of the top models: 15%

GPT-6.1 Sol: about $0.72
Gemini 4 Argon: about $1.99 (about $3.98 once the intro price ends). It writes a lot, about 62,000 tokens per task
Claude Opus 5.5: about $5.98

🏆 My take: Opus has the top independent score but costs the most. Argon wins on business automation and makes things up the least. Sol is way cheaper than both. snippet.title: ChatGPT Dots vs GrokBot
snippet.description:
OpenAI Dots vs Grok Bot: OpenAI just launched dots at DevDay 2026, an always-on AI agent that works for you 24/7. xAI launched almost the same thing, Grok Bot, seven weeks ago. I put them side by side to find out which one is actually better and which one you should pay for 👇

👥 Join my Skool community: [LINK]

Same questions for both: what can it do, how does it work with your apps, how many agents do you get, and what does it cost. I fill in a scorecard as we go, so you see exactly where each one wins. Spoiler: it's closer than you'd think.

🤖 Grok Bot (xAI)
✅ A whole team of bots (sales, inbox, invoices) that talk to each other in a group chat and pass work between them
✅ Logs into your apps like a human would (Gmail, your CRM, any website), so in theory it works with anything
✅ Teach it by showing it: do a task once (up to 10 minutes) and it saves it as a routine
✅ Comes with Cursor Pro ($20/month) or SuperGrok ($30/month), with a weekly allowance and extra usage billed on top
⚠️ Still in beta, and all your bots share one computer and the same logins

🟢 OpenAI dots
✅ Its own cloud computer and browser. It writes code, runs tests and sends you the pull request
✅ Powered by GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's top model
✅ Connects to 4,000+ apps through ChatGPT plugins, and lives in Slack and ChatGPT Space. Texting and phone calls are coming soon
✅ Included with ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium and Enterprise, and OpenAI says talking to your dot doesn't eat into your usage
✅ Stronger safety controls: you set which apps it can use and what it can do
⚠️ Only one dot for now (a team of dots is coming)
